picks.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage.
picks.abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems-a centuries-old practice2,3-causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800-2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48-99) mW m-2-equivalent to 2.7 (1.8-3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing-originating from 0.4-0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52-110) mW m-2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (-9 (-15--2) mW m-2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

picks.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor.
picks.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

picks.title: A unified framework for scalable differential testing for spatial omics
picks.abstract: A key challenge in spatial omics is identifying features whose values vary depending on both cell type and the surrounding cellular niche. Existing methods designed for spatial transcriptomic data do not generalize well to modalities beyond count-based data and do not scale efficiently to current data volumes. Here we introduce spotGLM, a mixture-aware generalized linear modeling framework for cell-type-specific differential testing across spatial modalities, and SPARROW, a power-preserving data distillation strategy for scalable inference. SpotGLM accommodates diverse data types including count-based gene expression, binomial isoform proportions and continuous chromatin accessibility scores within a unified statistical framework. We demonstrate the framework across spatial omics applications. On Visium HD data of colorectal cancer and mouse kidney, we recover cell-type-specific niche effects with serial-slice cross-platform validation. On long-read spatial RNA-seq data, we resolve cell-type-specific isoform switching in the mouse olfactory bulb. On spatial ATAC-seq data from mouse brain, we recover cell-type-specific spatial variation in regulatory motif accessibility.

picks.title: A blended digital parenting intervention for the prevention of sexual violence, exploitative sex, and maltreatment of children at scale in Tanzania: a cluster-randomised, controlled trial.

sections.objective: Childhood sexual, physical, and verbal violence are global public health priorities, affecting 1 billion children each year. ParentApp integrates sexual violence prevention into WHO-UNICEF's open-access Parenting for Lifelong Health programme, using innovative blended digital delivery. We aimed to test the efficacy of ParentApp in preventing sexual violence and maltreatment against adolescent-aged children and improving preventive mechanisms such as family mental health and adolescent-caregiver relationships.
sections.methods: This cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in 80 Tanzanian sub-wards. Participants were primary caregivers aged 18 years and older and their adolescents (aged 10-17 years). Sub-wards were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either ParentApp (intervention group) or a control WASHApp programme. Clusters were randomly assigned in blocks of six, stratified by urban versus rural location. Statisticians carrying out randomisation and data analysts were masked; it was not possible to mask participants or researchers. Intervention groups received a low-cost Android phone installed with ParentApp, a 12-module offline-first app, with one in-person orientation session and remote support via WhatsApp group chats, at a delivery cost of US$6 per family at scale, or $10 with 20% smartphone provision. Control groups received a low-cost Android phone installed with WASHApp, a 12-module offline-first app for water, sanitation, and hygiene, with one in-person orientation session. The primary outcomes were adolescent sexual violence victimisation and maltreatment and high-risk situations for sexual violence, assessed in all participants irrespective of uptake and engagement at 5 months and 18 months post-baseline. The trial was registered on March 14, 2023, with OSF (https://osf.io/t9fxz) and is completed.
sections.results: Between May 11 and Oct 9, 2023, 2692 caregiver-adolescent dyads were screened for study eligibility; 2396 adolescents (1217 [50·8%] female and 1179 [49·2%] male) and 2396 caregivers (1795 [74·9%] female and 601 [25·1%] male) were recruited. 2145 (89·5%) adolescents and 2252 (94·0%) caregivers were retained in the study and included in analyses at 18 months. Adolescent girls in ParentApp clusters had a substantial reduction in past-month sexual violence victimisation compared with those in control clusters (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0·43 [95% CI 0·21-0·86]; p=0·018), with no effect for boys (1·21 [0·59-2·43]; p=0·60). Past-month maltreatment (physical abuse, verbal abuse, and neglect) was lower in ParentApp clusters than in control clusters (adolescent report IRR 0·92 [0·88-0·96]; p<0·0001, caregiver report 0·87 [0·82-0·92]; p<0·0001). Past-month exposure to high-risk situations for sexual violence was lower in ParentApp clusters than in control clusters (adolescent girls IRR 0·87 [0·77-0·97]; p=0·012, adolescent boys 0·85 [0·79-0·91]; p<0·0001, caregiver report 0·81 [0·75-0·88]; p<0·0001). There were no reported adverse events.
sections.conclusion: A low-cost blended digital parenting programme in countries such as Tanzania could simultaneously reduce childhood sexual violence (for girls) and maltreatment and sexual violence risk situations (for girls and boys).

picks.title: Efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and stage 2-3 fibrosis: a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled study.

sections.objective: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH.
sections.methods: We did a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study conducted at 176 academic and community centres in 26 countries. We included adults (aged ≥18 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage 2 or stage 3 fibrosis. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) to receive either efinopegdutide (4 mg, 7 mg, or 10 mg), placebo, or open-label semaglutide 2·4 mg, all administered subcutaneously once weekly. Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete.
sections.results: Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. We randomly assigned 386 (23%) participants, of whom 381 (99%; 194 [51%] women and 187 [49%] men) received at least one dose of study intervention and were included in the analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). At week 52, MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis occurred in 31 (56%) of 55 participants in the 4 mg efinopegdutide group, 31 (63%) of 49 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 35 (61%) of 57 participants in the 10 mg efinopegdutide group versus seven (13%) of 53 participants in the placebo group (difference vs placebo 43·0 percentage points [95% CI 25·7 to 57·8; p<0·0001] for 4 mg, 49·5 percentage points [31·4 to 64·2; p<0·0001] for 7 mg, and 47·8 percentage points [30·7 to 62·0; p<0·0001] for 10 mg); 26 (53%) of 49 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. For the key secondary endpoint, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis occurred in 32 (43%) of 75 participants in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 39 (52%) of 75 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 26 (34%) of 77 participants in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group versus 16 (21%) of 77 participants receiving placebo (difference vs placebo 21·7 percentage points [7·1 to 35·7; p=0·0038] in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 30·4 percentage points [15·4 to 44·3; p<0·0001] in the efinopegdutide 7 mg group, and 13·0 percentage points [-1·2 to 26·8; p=0·072] in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group); 16 (25%) of 65 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. The most frequently reported adverse events with efinopegdutide were gastrointestinal, with the highest rates among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg. Adverse events leading to discontinuation of study intervention occurred more frequently among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg (nine [11%] of 79 participants) compared with the other doses of efinopegdutide (range 3-4%) or placebo (one [1%]).
sections.conclusion: Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH.

picks.title: Blood-Pressure-Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum.

sections.objective: Treatment for lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of cardiovascular events among persons at high risk. Whether this benefit extends to those at lower risk remains unclear.
sections.methods: We performed a meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomized trials comparing antihypertensive treatment (intervention) with placebo, an active comparator, or usual care (comparator). The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major cardiovascular event (fatal or nonfatal stroke, fatal or nonfatal ischemic heart disease, or heart failure resulting in death or hospitalization; composite outcome). Safety was assessed in trials that compared antihypertensive treatment with placebo or usual care, according to three prespecified composite outcomes: cardiovascular or hemodynamic events (palpitations, bradycardia, or hypotension), adverse renal events, and neurovestibular or fall-associated events. Participants were grouped into deciles according to predicted 5-year risk of a major cardiovascular event (median, 12.3%; lowest decile, 27%).
sections.results: We included data from 51 trials and 357,440 participants - 169,042 in the intervention group and 188,398 in the comparator group. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 19,202 participants (11.4%) in the intervention group and in 24,398 (13.0%) in the comparator group. The overall estimated hazard ratio for a major cardiovascular event per 5-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure was 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 0.92), with no evidence of variation across deciles. The absolute reduction in the 5-year cumulative risk of a major cardiovascular event was greater in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (2.6 vs. 0.4 percentage points), and the number needed to treat to prevent one major cardiovascular event over 5 years was lower in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (38 vs. 255). The incidence of a cardiovascular or hemodynamic event was 12.0 per 1000 person-years in the intervention group and 6.5 per 1000 person-years in the comparator group; the incidence of an adverse renal event was 3.3 and 2.2 per 1000 person-years, respectively; and the incidence of a neurovestibular or fall-associated event was 19.1 and 16.6 per 1000 person-years. The relative increase in the risk of each safety-outcome event with antihypertensive treatment as compared with placebo or usual care did not appear to vary across deciles.
sections.conclusion: Blood-pressure lowering was associated with a decreased risk of major cardiovascular events across the risk spectrum, including a predicted 5-year risk below 4%. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; PROSPERO registry number, CRD42018099283.).

picks.title: Physical activity coaching and text messaging for adults with mobility limitations (ComeBACK): hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of a physical activity coaching intervention compared with text messaging intervention and waitlist control in adults with mobility limitations.
sections.methods: Three arm, pragmatic, superiority, hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial. 512 community dwelling adults (≥18 years) who self-reported mobility limitations (difficulty or inability to walk 800 m, with or without a walking aid) but were still able to leave home without physical assistance from another person. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio to: a six month, multicomponent intervention including fortnightly physiotherapist delivered telephone coaching (coaching group, n=172); a six month, multicomponent intervention including regular unidirectional text messages (texting group, n=171); and no intervention for six months, followed by the six month text messaging intervention (waitlist control group, n=169). Participants and physiotherapists were unmasked to group allocation.
sections.results: Participants' mean age was 69 years (standard deviation (SD) 10 years) and 76% (n=388/511) were women. More than half (n=263/508, 51%) of participants reported multiple long term conditions as the main reason for their mobility limitation. At six months, mean daily steps were 931 higher (95% confidence interval 409 to 1452 steps; P=0.001) in the coaching group (mean 7256 (SD 3736) steps) compared with waitlist group (6526 (3003) steps); and 571 steps higher (58 to 1084, P=0.03) compared with the texting group (6529 (3029) steps). Mean daily steps in the texting group were 359 higher (-91 to 810, P=0.12) compared with the waitlist group, but this was not statistically significant. The number of adverse events was similar between groups (11/172 (6%) in the coaching group, 7/171 (4%) in the texting group, and 13/169 (8%) in the waitlist group) and none were serious.
sections.conclusion: A person centred coaching intervention produced modest increases in physical activity and was more effective than a less intensive texting intervention or no intervention among adults with mobility limitations.
sections.other: Health services and general communities across five Australian states, 19 December 2018 to 7 March 2023. The primary outcome was device measured mean daily steps at six months, analysed according to treatment allocation using all available data. Outcome assessors and data analysts were masked to group allocation.

picks.title: TECR palmitoylation triggers a necrotic cell death program driving acute liver injury.
picks.abstract: Acute liver injury caused by drug toxicity or immune activation remains a major clinical challenge with limited mechanistic understanding and few effective therapies. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized form of regulated cell death driven by palmitoylation of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident enzyme trans-2,3-enoyl-coenzyme A (CoA) reductase (TECR). We show that multi-site palmitoylation of TECR, redundantly catalyzed by the palmitoyl acyltransferases ZDHHC5 and ZDHHC2 and dynamically reversed by the depalmitoylase ABHD10, activates PERK-dependent ER stress signaling to trigger cell death. This cell death pathway is a TECR-dependent, palmitoylation-induced, ER stress-mediated necrotic cell death program (TPNCD). TPNCD contributes to liver injury in mouse models of acetaminophen- and concanavalin A-induced hepatotoxicity and is attenuated by hepatocyte-specific TECR ablation or by pharmacological inhibition of palmitoylation or ER stress signaling. Together, these findings establish TPNCD as a distinct, necrotic cell death pathway underlying acute liver injury and highlight new therapeutic entry points for hepatoprotection.

items.title: Reframing disease elimination: an update from the Lancet Commission on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
items.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with increasing global burden driven by population growth and ageing, persistent harmful exposures, and substantial health inequities. The Lancet Commission on COPD articulated an ambitious vision for disease elimination with prevention, early detection, and intervention. This Review revisits that vision, assesses progress since 2022, and calls for a broader commitment to lifelong lung health as an update of the Commission. Across seven sections, this Review advances a unified framework integrating the biology of lung development and ageing, precision medicine, patient-centred outcomes, and regulatory reform. COPD is not a single, uniform disease; rather, a biologically complex condition shaped by genetic, developmental, environmental, infectious, and behavioural factors across the entire life course. Effective prevention and care should therefore move beyond the detection and treatment of late physiological impairment toward earlier disease recognition, biological stratification, and interventions to preserve lung health, reduce symptoms, and prevent morbidity and premature mortality. The Review charts a path from reactive, late-stage management toward proactive, equitable, precision-based prevention and care. The central premise is unequivocal: the global burden of COPD can be substantially reduced. Success should be measured not only by gains in lung function and survival but also by improvements in daily functioning, quality of life, and wellbeing. In this expanded vision, COPD is no longer viewed solely as a chronic disease to be managed but as a preventable and modifiable condition within a broader commitment to lifelong lung health.

items.title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.

sections.objective: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
sections.methods: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327).
sections.results: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy.
sections.conclusion: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.

items.title: Izalontamab brengitecan for HR+/HER2- breast cancer in China (PANKU-Breast01): a randomised, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Patients with heavily pretreated hormone receptor-positive and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer have few treatment options. Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class, epidermal growth factor receptor and HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate that contains a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (Ed-04). The aim of PANKU-Breast01 was to compare the efficacy and safety of iza-bren versus chemotherapy in patients with pretreated HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
sections.methods: In this randomised, phase 3, open-label, multicentre study in 72 hospitals in China, patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer who had disease progression after endocrine therapy, cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg, administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks) or physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, 1·4 mg/m2; vinorelbine, 25 mg/m2; or gemcitabine, 1000 mg/m2, all administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks; or capecitabine, 1000-1250 mg/m2, administered orally twice daily on days 1-14 of each 3-week cycle). Stratified block randomisation was performed by an independent vendor using an interactive web response system, with stratification factors of number of previous lines of chemotherapy, CNS metastasis, and HER2 expression status. Patients, investigators, and site personnel involved in patient care and performing trial procedures were not masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review per RECIST (version 1.1) in the modified intention-to-treat population, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who had at least one dose of study drug. Median progression-free survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06343948, and is closed to recruitment.
sections.results: Between April 24, 2024, and June 6, 2025, 560 patients were screened, 177 were excluded, and 383 patients were randomly assigned and treated (190 were assigned to the iza-bren group and 193 were assigned to the chemotherapy group). All 383 participants in the study were female and of Chinese ethnicity. Median age was 54·0 years (IQR 47·0-60·0). At data cutoff (July 21, 2026), median follow-up for progression-free survival was 15·2 months (95% CI 13·9-16·8). Iza-bren significantly improved progression-free survival versus chemotherapy (log-rank p<0·0001), and median progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review was 8·2 months (95% CI 6·9-8·6) versus 4·0 months (2·9-4·3; HR 0·41 [95% CI 0·33-0·53]). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 162 (85%) patients in the iza-bren group versus 127 (66%) patients in the chemotherapy group, and haematological adverse events were the most common in both groups. For the treatment of haematological adverse events, 138 (73%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet-elevating agents, 28 (15%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet transfusion, and 18 patients (10%) in the iza-bren group received a blood transfusion. Two patients in the iza-bren group died due to treatment-related adverse events.
sections.conclusion: Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

items.title: Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair for Aortoesophageal Fistula Caused by Accidental Ingestion of a Press-Through Package Sheet: A Case Report.
items.abstract: An 88-year-old woman developed an aortoesophageal fistula after accidental ingestion of a press-through package sheet. Since endoscopic procedures failed to stop bleeding, thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) was performed, resulting in successful hemostasis. Although the patient finally died of sepsis associated with mediastinal infection, this case demonstrates the feasibility of TEVAR as a minimally invasive treatment option for this rare and life-threatening condition.

items.title: Superior Vena Cava Thrombosis in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Case Report of Two Patients.
items.abstract: Superior vena cava (SVC) thrombosis is a life-threatening condition, majorly it occurs when blood clots in a large vein, which carries blood to the heart. In chronic kidney disease (CKD) most of the SVC thrombosis cases are catheter-induced. We hereby report two CKD patients who were presented with superior vena cava (SVC) thrombosis and thrombosis in an internal jugular vein and innominate vein as diagnosed by CT angiography. Both the patients were under hemodialysis treatment through the Left radial cephalic AV fistula (AVF). Symptoms like breathlessness, hand pain and swelling, pallor, face swelling, puffy eyes, and body weakness were common in both patients. Clinically, the patients were managed with intravenous anticoagulants (low molecular Heparin) till recovery and discharged with oral anticoagulant (Apixaban).

items.title: Chemical speciation disparity underlies apparent preferential bioaccumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine in marine ecosystems.
items.abstract: Marine organisms strongly bioaccumulate iodine, making radioiodine transfer through food webs important for radiological risk assessment. Localized studies have reported higher 129I/127I atom ratios in marine biota than in seawater, suggesting apparent preferential accumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine over natural stable iodine. However, its broader occurrence and underlying mechanism remain unclear. Combining large-scale biological 129I/127I signatures with North Pacific seawater speciation data, we show that this enrichment spans multiple regions and is better explained by isotopic disequilibrium among seawater iodine species than by internal biological redistribution or trophic transfer. Major anthropogenic releases introduce radioiodine mainly as iodide, whereas stable iodine in open-ocean waters is dominated by iodate. Biological preference for iodide may link animal signatures more closely to iodide than to total iodine. Under nuclear accident scenarios, a chemical speciation-based calculation indicates that food chain models ignoring iodine speciation may underestimate radioiodine activity concentrations in marine animals by several-fold, up to approximately tenfold.

items.title: Cell-type identity, topography, and connectivity distinguish μ-opioid receptor neurons in prefrontal and somatosensory cortex.
items.abstract: The μ-opioid receptor (MOR), encoded by Oprm1, mediates both the pain-relieving and addictive effects of opioids. Despite the key role of cerebral cortex in pain perception and motivated behaviors, the identity of MOR-expressing cortical neurons remains unclear. To address this, we used intersectional genetic tools, single-cell RNA sequencing, viral tracing, and electrophysiology to characterize Oprm1-expressing neurons in the mouse cortex. We find Oprm1 expression in an assembly of inhibitory and pyramidal neuron subtypes preferentially located in deep layers, projecting to distinct thalamic nuclei and intracortically to layer 1. Furthermore, Oprm1+ neurons are concentrated in lateral areas, including the somatosensory cortex, rather than in medial prefrontal areas. This challenges prior assumptions, suggesting that MOR abundance in the medial prefrontal cortex may originate from thalamic inputs rather than local neurons. These findings define opioid-sensitive cortical circuits to study their contributions to opioid analgesia and addiction.

items.title: Identifying which patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer benefit most from androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (STOPCAP): a systematic review and meta-analysis of individual participant data.

sections.objective: Adding novel androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) to standard of care improves outcomes for patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), but whether benefits are consistent across patient subgroups remains uncertain. We aimed to assess whether ARPI effects vary according to participant or tumour characteristics, or by docetaxel use.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and meta-analysis (STOPCAP), we sought individual participant data for completed trials adding ARPIs to standard of care. Intention-to-treat, two-stage, common-effect meta-analysis of hazard ratios (HRs) were adjusted for a common set of covariates and docetaxel use. Main effects were based on overall survival. Interaction effects were based on progression-free survival (PFS) to maximise power, then overall survival whenever significant PFS interactions were found. Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), exploratory competing risk analyses of causes of death, and 5-year absolute effects were estimated overall and for key subgroups.
sections.results: Individual participant data were available from seven eligible trial comparisons (two comparisons from STAMPEDE, LATITUDE, PEACE-1, SWOG-S1216, ENZAMET, and TITAN) and 7778 participants (66% of total eligible). In the primary analysis of six trials (6467 participants and 3322 events), adding an ARPI improved overall survival (HR 0·66 [95% CI 0·62-0·710]; p<0·0001), with a 13% absolute improvement in 5-year survival. Similar results were observed for PFS. No evidence of effect variation was observed by ARPI class, docetaxel use, disease volume, Gleason score, performance status, or metastatic burden. ARPI effects on PFS varied by continuous age (interaction p=0·0005) and by age group (interaction p=0·0027), with patterns differing by ARPI class (biosynthesis versus receptor inhibitors: p=0·022) and similar results for overall survival. Based on individual participant data from three abiraterone trials (100% of eligible participants), effects on overall survival varied by age group (interaction p=0·0006), with an absolute 5-year improvement of about 15% for patients younger than 75 years but minimal benefit (about 1%) in those aged 75 years or older. Abiraterone improved 5-year PCSS across all age groups (11-18%), with a similar reduction in cumulative incidence of cancer deaths. However, in patients aged 75 years or older, abiraterone was associated with a 12% increase in 5-year cumulative incidence of non-cancer deaths. Based on limited individual participant data for receptor inhibitors (two trials; 35% of eligible participants), there was no clear evidence that effects on overall survival varied by age group (interaction p=0·078), and results from the STAMPEDE trial comparison of combined abiraterone and enzalutamide were similar.
sections.conclusion: Adding an ARPI to standard of care significantly improved overall survival for most patients with mHSPC. Although abiraterone improved cancer-specific survival for all, non-cancer mortality was increased among older patients. Further individual participant data are needed to fully assess the effects of androgen receptor inhibitors by age. Current data highlight the importance of considering age and comorbidities when selecting ARPI therapy.

items.title: Envudeucitinib in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (ONWARD1 and ONWARD2): results from two replicate, multicentre, double-blinded, placebo-controlled and active comparator-controlled, phase 3 randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: Safe and highly effective oral treatment options for patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis are scarce. Here, we aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of envudeucitinib (ESK-001), an investigational next-generation, highly selective, oral, allosteric tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor, in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
sections.methods: ONWARD1 (NCT06586112) and ONWARD2 (NCT06588738) are completed, replicate, multicentre, randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled and active comparator-controlled, phase 3 trials that enrolled patients in 333 sites (eg, research and medical centres, private practices, and hospitals) across 19 countries. Adults with a diagnosis of plaque psoriasis for at least 6 months, body surface area of at least 10%, and Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) of at least 12 were randomly assigned 2:1:1 to oral envudeucitinib 40 mg twice daily, placebo, or apremilast 30 mg twice daily for 24 weeks of treatment. At week 16, patients receiving placebo were transitioned to envudeucitinib. Coprimary endpoints were at least 75% improvement from baseline in Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI 75) and static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) of 0 or 1 at week 16 (envudeucitinib vs placebo). Secondary endpoints were assessed at weeks 16 and 24 (envudeucitinib vs placebo and/or apremilast). Safety assessments included adverse events and laboratory parameters.
sections.results: From July 25, 2024, to Dec 18, 2025, 912 and 859 patients were randomly assigned to ONWARD1 and ONWARD2, respectively (envudeucitinib, n=459 and n=433; placebo, n=230 and n=211; apremilast, n=223 and n=215). In both trials, coprimary and all key secondary endpoints were met (all p<0·0001). At week 16, envudeucitinib resulted in statistically significant PASI 75 responses versus placebo (ONWARD1: 351 [76·5%] of 459 vs 43 [18·7%] of 230; ONWARD2: 305 [70·4%] of 433 vs 29 [13·7%] of 211; both p<0·0001) and sPGA of 0 or 1 responses versus placebo (ONWARD1: 280 [61·0%] of 459 vs 23 [10·0%] of 230; ONWARD2: 248 [57·3%] of 433 vs 12 [5·7%] of 211; both p<0·0001). Up to week 16, 525 (59·0%) of 890 receiving envudeucitinib, 166 (37·6%) of 441 receiving placebo, and 224 (51·1%) of 438 patients receiving apremilast had one or more treatment-emergent adverse event. Up to week 24, 566 (63·6%) of 890 and 248 (56·6%) of 438 patients originally randomly assigned to envudeucitinib or apremilast had one or more treatment-emergent adverse event. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mostly mild or moderate and responsive to standard therapies; headache (97 [10·9%] of 890), nasopharyngitis (93 [10·4%] of 890), acne (60 [6·7%] of 890), and upper respiratory tract infection (57 [6·4%] of 890) occurred in at least 5% of patients receiving envudeucitinib during the trials. Up to week 16, serious adverse events occurred in 19 (2·1%) of 890 patients receiving envudeucitinib, five (1·1%) of 441 patients receiving placebo, and five (1·1%) of 438 patients receiving apremilast.
sections.conclusion: Envudeucitinib improved both skin signs and patient-reported outcomes, and maintained favourable tolerability, supporting its role as a promising oral treatment for patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

items.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs.
items.abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

items.title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing.
items.abstract: Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude (M) <3] are commonly modeled as simple circular ruptures, leaving the fine-scale spatial attributes of rupture dynamics unresolved. We used near-source distributed acoustic sensing to image the millisecond-scale rupture of an M 2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California's Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the M 2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

items.title: The original researchers would like a wordResearch: A Manifesto Peter N. Miller Princeton University Press, 2026. 256 pp.
items.abstract: Humanists pioneered scholarly research, but scientists get all the credit, argues a historian.

items.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake.
items.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude (Mw) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four Mw 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

items.title: In Science Journals.
items.abstract: Highlights from the Science family of journals.

items.title: In Other Journals.
items.abstract: Editors' selections from the current scientific literature.

items.title: Deception in motion.
items.abstract: Group motion may have evolved because it distorts what predators perceive.

items.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023-2024 record warming.
items.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023-2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean-atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

items.title: A tryptophan cation radical determines radical transfer kinetics and catalytic rate in a ribonucleotide reductase.
items.abstract: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) is the sole enzyme responsible for de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis for DNA replication and repair. In the Escherichia coli class Ia RNR, a radical must traverse 32 angstroms along a pathway composed of amino acids spanning β and α subunits to complete each turnover. By incorporating unnatural amino acids to alter reduction potentials of pathway tyrosine residues, we (i) perturb the rates of radical transfer and show that they match the rates of deoxynucleotide production and (ii) directly observe a tryptophan cation radical (W48+•) as a kinetically competent pathway intermediate. Together, these results establish that radical transfer through W48 in α2β2 is the rate-limiting process, which controls the enzymatic activity of E. coli RNR.

items.title: The absent-minded physicist who bested them allThe Man Who Broke Reality Philip Ball University of Chicago Press, 2026. 512 pp.
items.abstract: Despite his reputation for mumbling and bumbling, Niels Bohr's radical insights were unmatched.

items.title: Advancing undergraduates' skills for communicating science with the public.
items.abstract: Interdisciplinary communication and education research can help the next generation of science communicators address cultural conflicts.

items.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up.
items.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

items.title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels.
items.abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub-one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

items.title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity.
items.abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)-mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

items.title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer.
items.abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras-driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c-MYC-driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c-MYC-driven PLCs, Pten-deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten-deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8+ T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

items.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor.
items.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

items.title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer.
items.abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor-stroma borders harbor a MIF+ fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor-adipose borders, featured an FLT1+ endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

items.title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice.
items.abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

items.title: Giant-Cell Arteritis.
items.abstract: Giant-cell arteritis is a granulomatous vasculitis of large and medium-sized arteries that occurs almost exclusively in older adults. Suspected giant-cell arteritis warrants urgent diagnostic evaluation and, when ischemic risk is high, immediate treatment before diagnostic confirmation. Although glucocorticoids remain the cornerstone of therapy, treatment is frequently prolonged, associated with substantial toxic effects, and complicated by relapses. Advances in vascular imaging and insights into disease immunopathogenesis have expanded our understanding of disease heterogeneity and enabled the development of targeted therapies, particularly interleukin-6-receptor and Janus kinase inhibitors. Here, we review current concepts in the pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management of giant-cell arteritis and highlight areas of uncertainty that warrant further investigation.

items.title: Blood-Pressure-Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum.

sections.objective: Treatment for lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of cardiovascular events among persons at high risk. Whether this benefit extends to those at lower risk remains unclear.
sections.methods: We performed a meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomized trials comparing antihypertensive treatment (intervention) with placebo, an active comparator, or usual care (comparator). The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major cardiovascular event (fatal or nonfatal stroke, fatal or nonfatal ischemic heart disease, or heart failure resulting in death or hospitalization; composite outcome). Safety was assessed in trials that compared antihypertensive treatment with placebo or usual care, according to three prespecified composite outcomes: cardiovascular or hemodynamic events (palpitations, bradycardia, or hypotension), adverse renal events, and neurovestibular or fall-associated events. Participants were grouped into deciles according to predicted 5-year risk of a major cardiovascular event (median, 12.3%; lowest decile, 27%).
sections.results: We included data from 51 trials and 357,440 participants - 169,042 in the intervention group and 188,398 in the comparator group. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 19,202 participants (11.4%) in the intervention group and in 24,398 (13.0%) in the comparator group. The overall estimated hazard ratio for a major cardiovascular event per 5-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure was 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 0.92), with no evidence of variation across deciles. The absolute reduction in the 5-year cumulative risk of a major cardiovascular event was greater in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (2.6 vs. 0.4 percentage points), and the number needed to treat to prevent one major cardiovascular event over 5 years was lower in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (38 vs. 255). The incidence of a cardiovascular or hemodynamic event was 12.0 per 1000 person-years in the intervention group and 6.5 per 1000 person-years in the comparator group; the incidence of an adverse renal event was 3.3 and 2.2 per 1000 person-years, respectively; and the incidence of a neurovestibular or fall-associated event was 19.1 and 16.6 per 1000 person-years. The relative increase in the risk of each safety-outcome event with antihypertensive treatment as compared with placebo or usual care did not appear to vary across deciles.
sections.conclusion: Blood-pressure lowering was associated with a decreased risk of major cardiovascular events across the risk spectrum, including a predicted 5-year risk below 4%. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; PROSPERO registry number, CRD42018099283.).

items.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1-Negative Advanced NSCLC.

sections.objective: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.
sections.results: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

items.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3.
items.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

items.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor.
items.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal's assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing's most important challenges.

items.title: Nutritional interventions' impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings.
items.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

items.title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang.
items.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

items.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth.
items.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas-informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

items.title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines.
items.abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

items.title: Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Intermediate-High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.

sections.objective: Whether catheter-directed thrombolysis improves clinical outcomes in patients with intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, as compared with anticoagulation alone, is uncertain.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial, we randomly assigned patients with intermediate-high-risk acute pulmonary embolism (defined by hemodynamic stability, a simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index score of ≥1, and right ventricular dysfunction plus an elevated level of cardiac troponin or natriuretic peptide) in a 1:1 ratio to receive catheter-directed thrombolysis with alteplase plus anticoagulation therapy (thrombolysis group) or anticoagulation therapy alone (standard-care group). The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, recurrence of pulmonary embolism, or cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse within 7 days after randomization. Secondary outcomes included clinically relevant bleeding as defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium, major bleeding as defined in the Global Use of Strategies to Open Occluded Coronary Arteries guidelines, and intracranial hemorrhage.
sections.results: A total of 558 patients underwent randomization; 280 were assigned to the thrombolysis group, and 278 to the standard-care group. The median age was 64 years, and 40.9% were female. A primary-outcome event occurred in 2 patients (0.7%) in the thrombolysis group and in 19 patients (6.8%) in the standard-care group (relative risk, 0.10; 95% confidence interval, 0.02 to 0.44; P<0.001); this difference was driven mainly by the lower incidence of cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse in the thrombolysis group. By day 7, clinically relevant bleeding had occurred in 13 patients (4.6%) in the thrombolysis group and in 14 patients (5.0%) in the standard-care group (P = 0.85); major bleeding in 4 (1.4%) and 6 (2.2%), respectively (P = 0.54); and intracranial hemorrhage in 2 (0.7%) and none. One patient in the thrombolysis group died within 30 days, and 4 patients in the standard-care group died within 7 days.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with intermediate-high-risk acute pulmonary embolism, catheter-directed thrombolysis with alteplase plus anticoagulation therapy led to a lower risk of death from any cause, recurrent pulmonary embolism, or cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse within 7 days after randomization than anticoagulation therapy alone. (Funded by the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic and others; PRAGUE-26 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05493163; EudraCT number, 2022-002218-18; European Union Clinical Trials number, 2024-516144-25-00.).

items.title: Eplontersen for Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive, life-threatening disease caused by deposition of misfolded transthyretin (TTR). Eplontersen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces the production of hepatic TTR. The effect of eplontersen on ATTR-CM is unclear.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, international, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with ATTR-CM to receive subcutaneous eplontersen (45 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 140 weeks, in addition to standard treatment. The primary end point was a cumulative composite of death from cardiovascular causes and recurrent cardiovascular clinical events up to week 140. The effect of death from noncardiovascular causes on the primary analysis was assessed with a cumulative composite of death from any cause and cardiovascular events up to week 140.
sections.results: A total of 1432 patients underwent randomization and received at least one dose of the assigned intervention (715 patients in the eplontersen group and 717 in the placebo group). The mean age of the patients was 76.4 years, and 90.6% were men. A total of 381 primary end-point events occurred in 210 patients (29.4%) receiving eplontersen, and 392 events occurred in 231 patients (32.2%) receiving placebo (rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 1.09; P = 0.28). Death from cardiovascular causes, as a component of the primary end point, occurred in 74 patients in the eplontersen group and in 70 in the placebo group; there were 307 cardiovascular clinical events in the eplontersen group and 322 in the placebo group. The rate ratio for the composite of death from any cause and cardiovascular events was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.71 to 1.04). Serious adverse events occurred in 413 patients (57.8%) in the eplontersen group and in 426 (59.4%) in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with ATTR-CM, eplontersen therapy did not lead to a lower risk of a composite of death from cardiovascular causes and recurrent cardiovascular events than placebo up to 140 weeks. (Funded by Ionis Pharmaceuticals and AstraZeneca; CARDIO-TTRansform ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04136171.).

items.title: Successful Replacement of Collapsed Stent Graft at the Cephalic Arch for Salvaging Arteriovenous Fistulas.
items.abstract: Stent grafts, commonly used to manage cephalic arch stenosis in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula conduits, may lead to various complications. This article reports cases of collapsed stent grafts at the cephalic arch for which a novel approach is designed. The new approach includes surgically removing the collapsed stent graft and replacing it with a new stent graft using endovascular techniques. Three collapsed CoveraTM stent grafts at the cephalic arch were successfully replaced with VIABAHN® stent grafts, resulting in long-lasting clinical benefits. No procedure related complication was encounter. Replacing collapsed stent grafts at the cephalic arch with alternative stent grafts appears to be a feasible and effective strategy for salvaging affected arteriovenous fistulas.

items.title: The Rare Wrong Turn: Hybrid Management of Iatrogenic Vertebral Artery Injury During Internal Jugular Central Venous Catheter Placement.
items.abstract: BackgroundCentral venous catheter (CVC) insertion into the internal jugular vein (IJV) is a routine procedure, yet it carries a small but significant risk of arterial injury. While accidental arterial puncture occurs in 3.0%-9.4% of cases, inadvertent arterial cannulation is rare. Iatrogenic vertebral artery (VA) injury is exceptionally rare due to its protected anatomical position in the neck, but it carries a high risk of stroke and is difficult to manage with manual compression.Case DescriptionAn 89-year-old female required emergent IJV CVC placement following a cardiac arrest attributed to profound hypovolaemia. Computed tomography angiography suggested subclavian artery cannulation, however dynamic digital subtraction angiography (DSA) revealed a more complex trajectory: the CVC had penetrated the IJV and the adjacent VA, terminating in the subclavian artery. Removal of the catheter resulted in an immediate active contrast extravasation on DSA.ManagementDue to haemodynamic instability and a lack of onsite neurointerventional services, a hybrid management strategy was employed. A covered stent was deployed in the subclavian artery to seal the VA origin, followed by manual compression under fluoroscopic guidance to control retrograde flow from the distal VA.ConclusionThis case highlights that profound hypovolaemia can increase the risk of "through-and-through" venous punctures, leading to rare arterial injuries. In resource-limited settings where neurointerventional services were unavailable, a combination of proximal stenting and prolonged manual compression achieved haemostasis in this specific clinical setting.

items.title: Kidney Failure Risk Equation for Vascular Access Planning: A Practical Framework for Vascular Surgeons.
items.abstract: The timing and selection of vascular access (VA) in patients with chronic kidney disease are key determinants of hemodialysis outcomes. Conventional referral strategies based solely on estimated glomerular filtration rate may lead to premature or delayed arteriovenous fistula creation, resulting in unnecessary procedures or initiation of dialysis with a catheter. The Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE), which incorporates demographic and biochemical variables, provides a more individualized prediction of kidney failure risk within 2- and 5-year intervals. This review summarizes global validation studies of the KFRE, examines proposed risk thresholds for timely VA referral, and outlines a practical algorithm for incorporating the KFRE into multidisciplinary VA planning. From a vascular surgeon's perspective, the KFRE may serve not only as a referral tool but also as a decision-support framework for reassessing the appropriateness and timing of access creation after nephrology referral. In particular, the KFRE-based risk estimates should be interpreted alongside patient-specific factors, including age, frailty, comorbidities, life expectancy, vascular anatomy, dialysis modality preference, and transplant plans. This review also discusses competing-risk considerations, current limitations, and future directions for integrating the KFRE into routine clinical workflows.

items.title: Outcomes for Open, Endovascular, and Hybrid Treatment for Non-A Non-B Aortic Dissections: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: This review aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes of open (conventional arch repair, frozen elephant trunk), endovascular based treatment, hybrid, and conservative management for non-A non-B aortic dissection.
sections.results: Eighteen studies comprising 1 062 patients (mean age 55 years, 82% men) were included; 1 019 contributed to the pooled estimates. Pooled in hospital mortality was 4.6% (95% CI 2.2 - 9.6) after endovascular based treatment, 5.5% (2.6 - 11.3) after frozen elephant trunk, 7.8% (4.2 - 14.3) after hybrid repair, and 11.1% (4.0 - 27.1) with conservative management, with widely overlapping confidence intervals. Stroke ranged from 3.9% after endovascular based treatment to 9.7% with conservative management. Over 12 - 60 months mean follow up, cumulative mortality after discharge ranged from 3.1% (frozen elephant trunk) to 15.0% (conservative management), with 33.4% crossover to intervention. Retrograde type A dissection followed only stent graft based strategies (endovascular based treatment 3.4%); endoleak affected 15.7% of endovascular based treatment and 13.4% of hybrid patients. Certainty was very low overall.
sections.conclusion: In this synthesis, in hospital mortality was below 10% after endovascular based treatment, frozen elephant trunk and hybrid repair, each with a distinct complication profile relevant to treatment selection. These single arm proportions derive from populations selected by anatomy and operative fitness and are of very low certainty, and do not support estimation of comparative treatment effects.
sections.other: MEDLINE and Embase from inception to 9 September 2025, with a supplementary search for conservatively managed cohorts. This was a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions of non-randomised observational studies, in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO CRD42024534559). English language cohort studies and case series of ≥ 15 adult patients with non-A non-B dissection reporting predefined outcomes were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale). Proportions were pooled separately within each modality (random effects, logit transformation). No between modality comparison was made. Sensitivity analyses comprised leave one out, influence diagnostics, and a generalised linear mixed model. Certainty was rated using GRADE.

items.title: A randomized controlled trial of rotational thromboelastometry-guided blood component transfusion for difficult-to-treat variceal bleeding in ACLF.

sections.objective: Difficult-to-treat acute variceal bleeding (AVB) in acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) may require substantial red blood cell transfusions and coagulation-directed blood components (CDBCs), including fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate, and platelets, thereby predisposing to transfusion-related adverse events (TAEs). We assessed rebleeding, mortality, and CDBC requirements with rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM)-guided versus standard coagulation test (SCT)-guided transfusion strategies.
sections.methods: In this single-centre, randomised controlled trial, patients with ACLF and difficult-to-treat AVB were assigned (1:1) to ROTEM-guided or SCT-guided CDBC transfusion. The primary endpoint was first rebleeding by Day 42. Other endpoints included CDBC requirements, TAEs, and survival.
sections.results: Of 1,341 patients screened between November 2021 and January 2026, 766 had well-controlled bleeding and 313 were ineligible; 262 were randomised (ROTEM, n=132; SCT, n=130). Mean age was 45.1±11.6 years, MELD-Na 24.2±9.7, 64.5% had alcohol-associated ACLF, and 73% presented with shock. Bleeding sources were esophageal varices (85.9%) and gastric varices (14.1%); 113 patients had multiple bleeding sites, 112 had active spurting, and 37 had failure of endoscopic bleeding control, with 17 TIPS and 20 Danis-Ella stents insertions. First rebleeding by Day-42 occurred in 12.9% with ROTEM versus 13.9% with SCT (absolute risk difference [ARD], -1.0 percentage points [pp]; 95% CI: -9.2 to 7.3). All-cause mortality through the end of study was 31.1% versus 38.5%, respectively (ARD, -7.4 pp; 95% CI: -18.6 to 4.1). CDBCs were not required in 75.8% versus 52.3% (ARD, +23.5 pp; 95% CI:11.9 to 34.2). TAEs occurred in 6.8% versus 14.6% (ARD, -7.8 pp; 95% CI:-15.6 to -0.2).
sections.conclusion: ROTEM guidance reduced coagulation-directed blood component administration and TAEs compared with SCTs without compromising rebleeding or survival, supporting a restrictive approach in ACLF with difficult-to-treat AVB.

items.title: Nystagmus as a Key Determinant of Functional Vision and Eye-Related Quality of Life Impairment in Children Following Congenital Cataract Surgery in Northwest China.

sections.objective: Congenital cataract (CC) is a leading cause of treatable childhood blindness. Children frequently experience impairment in functional vision (FV) and eye-related quality of life (ER-QoL) even following cataract surgery. Current assessment of this issue is limited, especially in Northwest China. This study aims to evaluate FV and ER-QoL in children after CC surgery in Northwest China, identify their impact factors, and explore strategies for improvement.
sections.methods: Cross-sectional study. FV and ER-QoL of the participants were assessed using the Pediatric Eye Questionnaire (PedEyeQ), and their sociodemographic and clinical information were collected. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was employed to classify the severity of ER-QoL. Regression analysis was conducted to statistically analyze the impact factors on FV and ER-QoL.
sections.results: Children with CC showed significantly lower PedEyeQ scores than healthy children across all domains (P < 0.001), with the most pronounced deficit observed in adolescent Frustration/Worry (median score: 56 vs. 94). Proxy-reported FV scores were consistently lower than child self-reported scores in the 5-11-year age group (55 vs. 80). Nystagmus independently predicted FV impairment (adjusted Coeff: -11.04, 95% CI: -20.36 to -1.72; P = 0.022), whereas visual acuity did not.
