LPA classified three impairment profiles: mild (67.9%), moderate (22.2%), and severe (9.9%). In CC children, older age (OR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.12-2.96; P = 0.015), rural residence (OR = 5.61, 95% CI: 1.53-20.51; P = 0.009), and presence of nystagmus (OR = 10.74, 95% CI: 1.30-88.67; P = 0.027) were associated with an increased risk of severe ER-QoL.
sections.conclusion: CC children in Northwest China experience significant impairment in FV and ER-QoL. Nystagmus is a critical independent risk factor for both FV and ER-QoL. Older age and rural residence may increase the risk of severe impairment of ER-QoL. These findings highlight the need for child-centered assessment, nystagmus-focused interventions, and targeted resource allocation for rural populations in rehabilitation strategies.
sections.other: A total of 201 children aged 0-17 years who had undergone CC surgery were recruited at Xijing Hospital, Xi'an, China, between October 2022 and October 2023. In addition, 116 healthy children were included as controls. PedEyeQ domain scores, ER-QoL impairment profiles, and clinical and sociodemographic factors associated with impaired FV and ER-QoL.

items.title: Methodological and Reporting Quality of Systematic Reviews on Myopia Control: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.

sections.methods: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception to November 13, 2025. Eligible articles were systematic reviews of interventions for myopia control or prevention that evaluated efficacy, effectiveness, and/or safety and were published in English-language academic journals. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed methodological rigor using AMSTAR 2 and reporting completeness using PRISMA 2020. Citation impact was quantified using the Web of Science-reported Average per Year metric retrieved on September 5, 2026, and analysed as log(average citations per year + 1). The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169971).
sections.results: Ninety-one systematic reviews were included. Forty-five reviews (49%) were published in 2024 or 2025, and 56 (62%) had corresponding authors from China. AMSTAR 2 rated 51 reviews (56%) as critically low confidence, 26 (29%) as low, 6 (7%) as moderate, and 8 (9%) as high. Common limitations included inadequate protocol prespecification, incomplete literature searches, insufficient justification for excluded studies, and suboptimal risk-of-bias assessment. Mean PRISMA 2020 adherence was 75%, but certainty-of-evidence reporting was uncommon. Among 80 reviews with available citation data, citation impact did not differ across AMSTAR 2 confidence groups (P=0.38), but differed across intervention categories (P=0.01) and was weakly associated with journal impact factor (r=0.23; P=0.037).
sections.conclusion: Systematic reviews on myopia control have increased rapidly but frequently show important methodological limitations. Clinicians should interpret the conclusions of these reviews cautiously, with more attention to the underlying quality of the evidence synthesis. Future evidence syntheses should prioritize rigor over volume through adherence to AMSTAR 2 and PRISMA 2020 standards and the development of living systematic reviews with outcome-level certainty assessments updated as new evidence emerges.
sections.other: To evaluate the methodological confidence, reporting completeness, and citation impact of systematic reviews on interventions for myopia control. This study identifies priorities for improving methodological rigor and reporting completeness to support more reliable and clinically informative evidence synthesis in myopia.

items.title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations and Age-Related Structural Differences in Cyclic Nucleotide-Gated Channel-Related Retinopathies.

sections.objective: To characterize genotype-specific multimodal imaging phenotypes and expand the mutational spectrum of CNG channel-related inherited retinal diseases in a Chinese cohort, assess candidate structural biomarkers, and explore cross-sectional associations between age and ellipsoid zone (EZ) width in CNGA1- and CNGB1-associated retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
sections.methods: Multicenter cross-sectional observational study. 101 patients (202 eyes) with inherited retinal disease associated with biallelic or presumed biallelic variants in CNGA1, CNGB1, CNGA3, or CNGB3, and 35 age- and sex- matched healthy controls. Genomic variants and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA; logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution [logMAR]) were assessed. Ultra-widefield fundus autofluorescence and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) were analyzed. Mixed-effects models and exploratory segmented regression examined structure-function and age-EZ width associations.
sections.results: Sixty-two distinct variants were identified across four CNG genes, including two exon-level deletions. CNGA1 c.253del and CNGB1 c.217+5G>C were the most frequent variants in their respective genes. Rod-dominant genotypes exhibited centripetal hypoautofluorescence with a parafoveal hyperautofluorescent ring, whereas CNGA3-ACHM showed increased foveal autofluorescence. OCT-defined foveal hypoplasia (FH) morphology differed across genotype groups: CNGA1-RP and CNGB1-RP predominantly showed low-grade classical FH morphology, whereas the small CNGA3-ACHM and CNGB3-ACHM cohorts more frequently showed atypical FH morphology with outer retinal disruption. Both CNGA1-RP and CNGB1-RP demonstrated reduced parafoveal retinal and choroidal thickness versus controls (P < .001). In CNGA1-RP, EZ width showed the strongest single-predictor association with BCVA (R² = 0.68) and remained associated after adjustment for age and central foveal thickness (β per 1000 μm, -0.260 logMAR; 95% confidence interval, -0.353 to -0.168; P < .001). Exploratory segmented regression suggested an age-associated EZ width threshold near 41 years; the age-group difference was larger in the CNGA1-RP than in the CNGB1-RP group (interaction P = .030).
sections.conclusion: CNG channel-related retinopathies had distinct genotype-specific imaging patterns. EZ width merits further evaluation as a candidate structural biomarker, particularly in CNGA1-associated RP. The exploratory age-associated pattern in EZ width near 41 years requires longitudinal validation before informing progression estimates or therapeutic timing.
sections.other: Genotype-specific imaging patterns, BCVA, EZ width, retinal and choroidal thickness, and variant spectrum.

items.title: Safety and vision outcome after interventions for symptomatic vitreous floaters, a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: We evaluated the major adverse events and visual quality-related outcomes of pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) and Neodymium:Yttrium-Aluminum-Garnet (Nd:YAG) laser vitreolysis in the management of symptomatic vitreous floaters and vision-degrading myodesopsia. Twenty studies were included in the quantitative synthesis of safety and visual quality outcomes. Pooled analysis showed only a modest best-corrected visual acuity improvement (-0.042 logMAR), which was supportive rather than a central efficacy measure, whereas contrast sensitivity function outcomes were too heterogeneous to pool (I² = 94%) and vision-related quality of life data came from 1 study. Nevertheless, greater clinical attention should be devoted to patient-reported outcome measures other than emphasizing high-contrast visual acuity alone. We found adverse events like rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, retinal tear, and vitreous hemorrhage uncommon in both groups, whereas cataract progression constituted the key distinguishing safety outcome between the 2 treatments: the pooled incidence was 15.63% among phakic eyes following PPV and 2.68% after Nd:YAG vitreolysis, which highlighted the need for personalized treatment selection according to phakic status during clinical management. Our results were limited by the follow-up duration, lack of head-to-head comparison trials, heterogeneity in outcome definitions, ceiling effects and poor specificity in outcome measures, selection bias among patients allocated to each treatment.

items.title: Research Advances in Diabetic Keratopathy.
items.abstract: We systematically synthesize recent advances (primarily January, 2020, to June, 2026, with additional references from other years as appropriate) in the pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostic techniques, and treatment strategies for diabetic keratopathy. Emphasizing the importance of early identification and targeted intervention, we propose a novel systematic framework integrating the "mechanism-phenotype-therapy" continuum. Diabetes mellitus damages corneal nerves, endothelial cells, and epithelium through multiple complex mechanisms, leading to corneal hypoesthesia, delayed epithelial healing, and reduced transparency. Advances in diagnostic technologies, particularly in vivo confocal microscopy, have enabled quantitative assessment of corneal nerve morphology, establishing it as a sensitive biomarker for diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Current therapeutic approaches, however, remain largely limited to symptomatic management, despite the regulatory approval of mechanism-based therapies such as cenegermin (EMA 2017; FDA 2018) for neurotrophic keratitis. Emerging strategies targeting neuroprotection, immunomodulation, metabolic pathways, and regenerative medicine show considerable promise. We critically appraise the evidence base, identifying consensus, controversies, and knowledge gaps that require future investigation. Therefore, diabetic keratopathy management requires a multifaceted approach encompassing early diagnosis, mechanistic elucidation, and personalized treatments. Future research should focus on deciphering underlying molecular pathways, particularly neuro-immune crosstalk, and translating these findings into precise diagnostic tools and effective multi-targeted therapies to improve corneal health in diabetic patients.

items.title: Dissecting Age-Related Macular Degeneration: From Human Histology to Clinical Imaging and Therapeutic Translation.
items.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains classified largely by visible lesions, yet human histology shows that clinical appearance only partially reflects the underlying biology. This review integrates historical pathology, donor-eye morphometry, lipid biochemistry, and modern multimodal imaging to reframe AMD as progressive failure of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), Bruch's membrane (BrM), and choriocapillaris (CC) exchange unit. A deposit-centric, compartment-resolved approach is proposed, emphasizing that drusen, basal linear deposit (BLinD), basal laminar deposit (BLamD), subretinal drusenoid deposits (SDD), acquired vitelliform lesions, calcified drusen, geographic atrophy (GA), and macular neovascularization (MNV) represent distinct but interacting expressions of interface dysfunction. Human histology demonstrates that clinically visible drusen often underestimate disease burden because diffuse, lipid-rich BLinD may extend widely within BrM while remaining largely occult on routine optical coherence tomography (OCT). Conversely, OCT-conspicuous elevations may contain heterogeneous mixtures of lipid, matrix elements such as collagen, mineralization, cellular debris, and remodeling tissue, limiting the specificity of size-based grading. Fixation, staining, postmortem interval, eccentricity, and ex vivo imaging registration determine what lesions can be recognized and how histologic findings can be translated into clinical imaging biomarkers. Lipoprotein-like particle retention, esterified cholesterol accumulation, complement dysregulation, RPE stress responses, CC attenuation, and vascular remodeling are discussed as inter-related mechanisms rather than independent pathways. AMD heterogeneity is best explained by parallel deposit systems, especially basal sub-RPE/BrM deposits and apical subretinal deposits, whose topography, composition, and vascular context influence progression toward atrophy or neovascular disease. Existing Wisconsin, AREDS, AREDS2, and Beckman classifications remain valuable for clinical assessment, reproducibility and population risk prediction, but they should be complemented by a biological overlay based on compartment, configuration, RPE state, vascular context, and topography. This framework has direct implications for prognosis, imaging interpretation, and trial design, because therapies targeting complement, lipid trafficking, inflammation, or vascular pathways are likely to show clearer effects when enrollment and endpoints are aligned with active lesion biology. By linking lesion identity to mechanism, it may also improve patient stratification and clarify why structurally similar eyes follow divergent clinical trajectories. A deposit-centric classification may therefore bridge human histology, clinical imaging, and therapeutic translation in AMD. Emerging high-resolution OCT may further narrow the histology-imaging gap by revealing previously unresolved microstructural deposit phenotypes, including presumed basal laminar deposit (BLamD) and associated RPE abnormalities.

items.title: Human retinal organoid integration into 3D neural tissue models - an emerging opportunity.
items.abstract: Human retinal and brain organoids are transforming research into human neural development, disease and regenerative medicine, reproducing key structural, molecular and functional features of the retina and brain and providing an experimentally accessible model. However, these systems have largely been developed in isolation, limiting their ability to model the long-range neuronal connectivity that underlies visual function and the shared mechanisms of retinal and central nervous system disease. Recent advances in assembloid technologies, tissue engineering and computational analysis now make the generation of integrated human eye-brain models an increasingly realistic goal. In this review, we focus on the integration of retinal and brain organoids to reconstruct elements of the human visual pathway. We discuss advances in retinal and brain organoid differentiation that improve maturation, reproducibility and physiological fidelity, including vascularization, glial incorporation, extracellular matrix engineering and functional electrophysiological assessment. We examine strategies for assembling multi-regional neural tissues to promote retinal ganglion cell projection, target-specific connectivity and circuit formation and consider how eye-brain assembloids could provide platforms to investigate retinal and neurological disorders while accelerating therapeutic discovery and human tissue-based preclinical testing. Finally, we discuss the technical and biological challenges that remain, including incomplete maturation, standardisation, scalability and functional validation, and highlight how advances are likely to drive the next generation of physiologically relevant human visual system models. By integrating developments across retinal organoids, brain organoids and assembloid technologies, this review outlines a framework for modelling human eye-brain connectivity and defines the opportunities and challenges that will shape this emerging field.

items.title: Delayed oxygen saturation recovery after the 6-minute walk test: Prognostic implications for COPD patients.

sections.methods: In this prospective observational cohort, 512 consecutive patients were recruited through the Galdakao University Hospital Respiratory Service and underwent pulmonary function and quadriceps strength assessments, multisensor accelerometry, and a 6MWT. Desaturation was defined as a ≥3% decrease in SpO2 from baseline during the 6MWT; SpO2-RT was the time from test completion until SpO2 returned to baseline.
sections.results: Of the 512 enrolled patients 25% were female. Those who experienced oxygen desaturation during the 6MWT exhibited significantly worse pulmonary function (FEV1%, RV%, IC/TLC and DLCO%) (p <.0001), higher fibrinogen levels (p =.01), lower quadriceps strength (p =.02), reduced PA (p <.0001), and a shorter distance walked (p <.0001). Within the desaturation sub-cohort, differences were analysed based on a SpO2-RT cut-off ≥ 80 seconds. Patients with a prolonged SpO2-RT exhibited more severe pulmonary function impairment (p values ranging from .02 to <.0001), significantly lower PA (p =.001), and shorter distance 6MWT (p <.0001). During the 3-year follow-up increased SpO2-RT was associated with increased mortality (p =.03) and hospitalizations (p =.0003). In the adjusted analyses, prolonged SpO2-RT was associated with an approximately twofold higher risk of both hospitalization (p = .02) and mortality (p =.04).
sections.conclusion: A prolonged SpO2-RT ≥ 80 identifies a COPD phenotype characterized by diminished respiratory reserve and an increased risk of subsequent exacerbation-related hospitalizations and all-cause mortality. SpO2-RT is a simple, accessible metric that enhances the prognostic utility of the standard 6MWT.
sections.other: The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is a fundamental instrument in the clinical management of COPD patients, yet the prognostic value of specific physiological parameters during the recovery phase remains underexplored. This study aimed to determine whether the recovery time of oxygen saturation (SpO2-RT) following a 6MWT is associated with long-term prognosis (death and hospitalizations) in a cohort of patients with COPD.

items.title: Respiratory Therapists' Intentions to Leave their Current Position.

sections.objective: Many respiratory therapy departments face staffing shortages with high turnover rates. What drives turnover among respiratory therapists (RTs) is unclear.
sections.methods: We performed a planned secondary analysis of a multicenter, multinational study of RT burnout. We compared those with an intent to leave score ≥ 50 to those with a score < 50 and report odds ratios OR with 95% confidence intervals (CI) using univariable logistic regression.
sections.results: We received 1,014 responses and 536 (53%) had an intention to leave score ≥ 50. Statistically significant factors associated with intention to leave included: emotional exhaustion (OR 13.2), felt other RTs were burned out (OR 6.4), felt their workload was too high (OR 3.9), exposure to incivility (OR 3.4), unable to complete all their work (OR 2.4), inadequate staffing (OR 2.3), activities restricted due to illness (OR 2.0), worked 31-50 hours in the ICU (OR 1.6), bachelor's degree (OR 1.4) and missed work for any reason (OR 1.4). Statistically significant factors associated with low intention to leave included: felt valued by their organization (OR 0.1), a positive leadership score (OR 0.2), agreed their director/manager cared about them as a person (OR 0.2), satisfaction with total compensation (OR 0.3), < 2 years as an RT (OR 0.4), and spending their time performing high value activities (OR 0.6).
sections.conclusion: Over half of RTs had an intention to leave. Emotional exhaustion, incivility, leadership, staffing, workload, hours worked in the ICU, bachelor's degree, and perceived value were all associated with intent to leave while hours worked, and patient population were not associated with intent to leave.
sections.other: What variables are associated with RT's intention to leave their current position.

items.title: Baseline anti-gliadin antibody positivity and 24-week response to ritlecitinib in moderate-to-severe alopecia areata: A retrospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Pretreatment markers of response to ritlecitinib in alopecia areata (AA) remain limited. To evaluate whether baseline anti-gliadin antibody (AGA) positivity is associated with week-24 response to ritlecitinib.
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort included 80 patients with moderate-to-severe AA treated with ritlecitinib 50 mg daily. Outcomes were a ≥75% improvement in Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score relative to baseline (SALT75) and SALT ≤20 at week 24. Associations were assessed using logistic regression with adjustment for clinical factors. Baseline serum protein profiles were compared between AGA-positive and AGA-negative patients.
sections.results: Of the 80 patients, 28 (35.0%) were AGA positive. At week 24, SALT75 rates were 60.7% versus 34.6%, and SALT ≤20 rates were 71.4% versus 50.0%, in AGA-positive versus AGA-negative patients. Adjusted odds ratios were 4.82 (95% CI, 1.42-16.32) and 6.73 (95% CI, 1.24-36.54), respectively. Among 44 patients with baseline proteomic data, no protein remained significant after correction for multiple testing.
sections.conclusion: Pretreatment AGA positivity was associated with better week-24 response to ritlecitinib after adjustment for clinical factors.
sections.other: Retrospective, single-center design and modest sample size.

items.title: Rucaparib versus docetaxel or second-generation androgen pathway inhibitor therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: final overall survival and safety from the phase III TRITON3 study.

sections.objective: We report final overall survival (OS) from TRITON3, evaluating rucaparib versus physician's choice (docetaxel or androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor [ARPI]) in chemotherapy-naive men with BRCA/ATM-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) progressing after one prior ARPI. We previously reported that rucaparib significantly improved radiographic progression-free survival (PFS) for patients with BRCA mutations, including versus docetaxel and ARPI only.
sections.methods: This open-label, phase 3 trial randomized 405 patients (302 with BRCA mutations) 2:1 to receive rucaparib or physician's choice. Crossover from physician's choice to rucaparib was allowed after confirmed radiographic disease progression. OS was a key secondary endpoint. The primary endpoint and other key secondary endpoints were reported previously.
sections.results: For rucaparib vs physician's choice, median OS was 23.2 versus 21.2 months (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.68-1.20; median follow-up, 44 months; BRCA subgroup), was 22.8 versus 21.7 months (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.78-1.26; ITT), and was similar vs docetaxel or ARPI alone. PSA response rates (BRCA subgroup) were 54.7% (rucaparib) versus 26.7% (physician's choice). Of the 76% eligible to crossover in the BRCA subgroup (n = 53), median radiographic PFS from rucaparib initiation was 6.2 months (n = 30) and 18.1 months (n = 23) for those receiving initial docetaxel or initial ARPI, respectively. With long-term follow-up, acute myeloid leukemia/myelodysplastic syndrome incidence was 1%.
sections.conclusion: Although rucaparib demonstrated significant increases in radiographic PFS and response rate, OS was similar in both arms, albeit most patients crossed over. Thus, rucaparib is a safe and beneficial treatment option against BRCA-mutated mCRPC.

items.title: Determinants and Clinical Impact of Medication Non-Adherence in Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease: A Prospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Adherence to guideline-recommended medical therapy reduces the risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with lower extremity peripheral artery disease (LE-PAD), yet adherence remains low. This study aimed to prospectively identify determinants of therapeutic non-adherence among unselected patients with LE-PAD seen in routine practice.
sections.methods: We conducted a single-centre, prospective study of consecutive patients with symptomatic LE-PAD seen at Amiens-Picardie University Hospital between June and December 2025. Adherence was assessed at inclusion using the self-administered Girerd questionnaire (good, moderate, or poor adherence) and re-assessed at 3 months. Determinants of non-adherence were identified using ordinal logistic regression. Associations with MALE (Firth's penalized logistic regression adjusted for a priori confounders) and MACE (Fisher's exact test) were assessed at 3 months, and at 6 months as a sensitivity analysis.
sections.results: Of 174 patients included, 171 completed the Girerd questionnaire and were analysed (median age 69 years, 73.7% male): 31.0% had good adherence, 40.4% moderate, and 28.7% poor adherence. Diabetes (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.35, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.26-4.38) and obesity (aOR 2.24, 95% CI 1.06-4.74) were independently associated with poorer adherence, whereas regular alcohol use was associated with better adherence (aOR 0.19, 95% CI 0.07-0.55). Poor adherence increased from 28.7% to 40.0% at 3 months (p=0.009). At 3 months, all 5 MACE occurred in poorly adherent patients (10.9% vs. 0%, p=0.002), and poor adherence was non-significantly associated with MALE (aOR 2.26, 95% CI 0.73-7.71); at 6 months, this association was significant (aOR 4.14, 95% CI 1.47-12.9).
sections.conclusion: In this real-world, unselected LE-PAD population, diabetes and obesity were independent determinants of poor therapeutic adherence, which was associated with early cardiovascular events and with limb events at 6 months. These findings identify a distinct high-risk patient profile that could be screened at first consultation to guide individualized adherence-support interventions.

items.title: Challenges and Management Strategies for Endovascular Repair of Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm in Patients with Hostile Iliac Artery Anatomy: A Literature Review.

sections.objective: Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is widely used for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (iAAAs), but its long-term durability remains limited by endoleaks, stent-graft migration, iliac limb complications, and secondary interventions. Although previous studies have mainly focused on the proximal aortic neck, the distal iliac landing zone is equally important for durable sealing, fixation, and pelvic perfusion. Hostile iliac artery anatomy (HIA) may impair device delivery, contralateral gate cannulation, iliac limb deployment, and distal sealing, thereby increasing the risk of type Ib endoleak, iliac limb occlusion, and pelvic ischemic complications.
sections.methods: This review summarizes the anatomical features, procedural challenges, and contemporary management strategies for HIA during EVAR. Particular emphasis is placed on a problem-oriented framework linking specific iliac anatomical features to major technical challenges, including difficult access, cannulation failure, inadequate distal sealing, limb instability, and internal iliac artery involvement. Current endovascular, hybrid, and open adjunctive strategies are reviewed, including low-profile devices, vessel preparation, crossed-limb deployment, contralateral snare cannulation, bell-bottom limbs, iliac branch devices, parallel grafting, fenestration techniques, and internal iliac artery reconstruction, among others.
sections.conclusion: HIA remains a major determinant of technical complexity and long-term durability after EVAR. Management should extend beyond aneurysm exclusion to ensure stable distal sealing, iliac limb patency, and preservation of at least one internal iliac artery whenever feasible. Although multiple endovascular and hybrid strategies have expanded treatment options, high-level comparative evidence remains limited, and many techniques are supported mainly by retrospective or single-center data. Future advances should focus on standardized technical protocols, prospective multicenter evidence, and next-generation devices with broader anatomical applicability. In particular, device profiles, diameters, lengths, and branch configurations should be better adapted to populations with shorter iliac segments and smaller vessel diameters, especially Asian patients, to reduce device-anatomy mismatch and improve long-term outcomes.

items.title: True Lumen Guided Stent Sizing Predicts Distal Aortic Remodeling After ATAAD Repair.

sections.objective: Descending thoracic aorta (DTA) remodeling is a critical determinant of long-term survival after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair. Despite the widespread use of the frozen elephant trunk (FET) technique, quantitative evidence for stent graft sizing based on true lumen (TL) dimensions remains scarce. This study investigated whether the difference between the stent and true lumen diameters (Δ) serves as a reliable predictor of late DTA remodeling.
sections.methods: 147 ATAAD patients (2018-2022) were analyzed. Preoperative CTA was used to measure true lumen diameter (TL), false lumen diameter (FL) or total aortic diameters at the proximal landing zone. The parameter Δ was defined as the implanted stent graft diameter minus the preoperative TL diameter. Late DTA remodeling was defined by a >20% increase in TL proportion, FL thrombosis, and the absence of significant enlargement of the total aortic diameter. Multivariable logistic regression and ROC analysis were employed to evaluate the predictive value of Δ and identify an optimal clinical threshold.
sections.results: ΔWas independently associated with late DTA remodeling (adjusted OR 1.163 per 1-mm increase; P = 0.010). ROC analysis identified 9 mm as the optimal cutoff. Patients with Δ > 9 mm had higher remodeling rates than those with Δ ≤ 9 mm (90.6% vs. 77.1%; P = 0.031). Subgroup analyses showed a generally consistent direction of association across stent-graft sizes, although statistical significance varied among subgroups. This finding was confirmed in an external validation cohort of 42 subsequent patients treated at our center.
sections.conclusion: A Δ threshold > 9 mm was associated with a higher likelihood of favorable late distal aortic remodeling after FET, providing a simple, evidence-based benchmark for preoperative planning.

items.title: Fear of amputation and death and quality of life in patients with intermittent claudication.

sections.objective: Intermittent claudication caused by peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with risk of major amputation and death, but it is unclear to what extent patients fear these complications and whether these fears influence quality of life (QoL) and risk of events. This study assessed the prevalence of fear of amputation and death amongst patients with intermittent claudication, and examined the association of these fears with QoL and risk of major amputation and death.
sections.methods: In this prospective cohort study enrolling 354 patients, fear of amputation and death from PAD were assessed with two questionnaire items. Primary outcome was the combined incidence of major amputation and death. Secondary outcomes were disease-specific QoL assessed by PADQOL, mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
sections.results: Of the 354 patients, 202 (57.1%) either strongly agreed (76, 21.5%), agreed (67, 18.9%) or somewhat agreed (59, 16.7%) that they feared amputation. A total of 151 of the 354 patients (42.7%) indicated that they strongly agreed (50, 14.1%), agreed (35, 9.9%) or somewhat agreed (66, 18.6%) that they were afraid of dying because of PAD. Patients with higher scores for fear of amputation and death had significantly lower QoL scores. Median follow-up was 2.3 (interquartile range: 1.3, 7.0) years, during which time 60 (16.9%) deaths, 6 (1.7%) major amputations and 50 (14.1%) MACEs occurred. A one unit increase in the fear score was associated with an increased risk of both major amputation or death (unadjusted HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02, 1.19, p=0.010; risk factor adjusted HR 1.10, 1.01, 1.19, p=0.027) and death alone (unadjusted HR 1.09, 95% CI 1.01, 1.18, p=0.029; risk factor adjusted HR 1.09, 1.00, 1.19, p=0.044), but not MACE.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with intermittent claudication fear of amputation and death are common and associated with poorer QoL and increased risk of these events.

items.title: Frontal ripples cooperate with mixed-selectivity neurons for compositional sequence control.
items.abstract: In mammals, bursts of high-frequency local field potential oscillations, or "ripples," often accompany sequential spatiotemporal associations. However, whether and how ripples support the control of sequences remains largely unexplored. We trained two macaque monkeys to perform a visuospatial sequence working memory task that required flexible assembly and manipulation of sequence constituents. We found that frontal ripples preferentially cooccurred with mixed-selectivity neurons that encoded multiple sequence items and that ripple rates predicted the neurons' contributions to sequence representations. Crucially, co-ripples and phasic synchronization with local spiking activity delineated a potential time window for coordinating or binding sequence constituent information. Furthermore, this binding process could be generalized to longer sequences and even sequence reconstruction. Thus, coupling of frontal cortical ripples with mixed-selectivity neurons underlies sequence formation and reorganization in working memory.

items.title: The identity gene Fezf2 is repurposed postnatally to specify inhibitory input in an activity-dependent manner.
items.abstract: The development and function of cortical circuits require an appropriate balance of excitation and inhibition. Pyramidal cells, the principal excitatory cells in the cerebral cortex, recruit inhibitory synapses in proportion to their activity. How each pyramidal cell subtype achieves the cell-type-specific levels of inhibition it requires is unknown. Here we show in mice that a neuronal identity gene is repurposed postnatally to regulate inhibitory connectivity. Fezf2, which encodes a transcription factor that establishes the identity of extratelencephalic pyramidal cells in layer 5 during embryonic development, is regulated by activity after birth only in those neurons. Activity-dependent FEZF2 controls the number of inhibitory synapses formed by parvalbumin-expressing interneurons through regulation of the cell-surface protein Cadherin-22. Our findings reveal that a gene specifying neuronal subtype identity is redeployed to control how activity refines wiring, giving activity-dependent circuit development its cell-type specificity.

items.title: A brown planthopper effector promotes virulence by targeting the rice resistance protein BPH6.
items.abstract: Breeding resistant crops provides an effective and sustainable approach to control insect pest, yet the emergence of virulent insect populations continues to undermine this strategy. The molecular basis by which insects overcome host plant resistance remains largely unknown. Here we identified GPS6, the Gut Protein Suppressing BPH6 in brown planthopper (BPH). GPS6 is highly expressed in the gut of virulent BPHs and orally delivered into rice to suppress the resistance conferred by the resistance gene Bph6. GPS6 specifically binds to a variable insertion region (amino acids 586-790) of BPH6, thus disrupting the association of BPH6-OsEXO70H3, impairing exocytosis and attenuating defense-related hormone signaling and lignin deposition. Conversely, in susceptible rice, Gps6 triggers defense responses and inhibits insect feeding, imposing a fitness cost. Our findings uncover a previously unrecognized effector-mediated mechanism by which an insect neutralizes a plant resistance protein, informing strategies for durable pest resistance in crops.

items.title: Rafutrombopag for chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia in patients with solid tumours: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia can disrupt planned chemotherapy through treatment delay, dose reduction, discontinuation, or rescue therapy. We assessed the efficacy and safety of rafutrombopag, an oral thrombopoietin receptor agonist, in patients with solid tumours and established chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia associated with platinum-based chemotherapy.
sections.methods: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial done at 43 sites in China, adults aged 18-75 years with solid tumours, platelet count less than 75 × 109/L, and an actual thrombocytopenia-related chemotherapy delay of at least 7 days associated with platinum-based combination chemotherapy were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to continuous rafutrombopag, switch rafutrombopag, or placebo. During the pre-chemotherapy correction period, patients in the continuous and switch groups received 7·5 mg oral rafutrombopag once daily and patients in the placebo group received matching placebo during the correction period; patients in the switch group changed to placebo when cycle 1 chemotherapy began. The protocol target for resuming chemotherapy was a platelet count of at least 100 × 109/L. Response was assessed within 14 days; patients who had not responded by day 14 could receive rescue therapy, resume chemotherapy, or both at the investigator's discretion. During two subsequent 3-week chemotherapy cycles, the continuous group continued platelet-guided rafutrombopag (2·5 mg dose-level adjustments; maximum 15 mg once daily), and the switch and placebo groups received matching placebo. The primary endpoint was a composite response, defined as platelet response (platelet count of at least 100 × 109/L) within 14 days after starting study treatment, completion of the first on-study chemotherapy cycle using the same chemotherapy regimen as before enrolment, platelet count of at least 75 × 109/L on cycle 1 day 21, and no platelet-increasing rescue therapy before cycle 1 day 21. Efficacy was analysed in the intention-to-treat population and safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05864014) and is complete.
sections.results: Between April 27, 2023, and March 3, 2025, 213 patients were randomly assigned to continuous rafutrombopag (n=70), switch rafutrombopag (n=72), or placebo (n=71). Overall, 211 (99%) patients entered the pre-chemotherapy correction period and received at least one dose of study treatment. The median age of enrolled patients was 61 years (IQR 56-68), 112 (53%) were male and 101 (47%) were female. 204 (96%) of 213 patients were Han Chinese and nine (4%) were from other ethnic groups. The primary endpoint was met by 53 (76%) of 70 patients in the continuous group, 35 (49%) of 72 in the switch group, and 28 (39%) of 71 in the placebo group. Compared with placebo, the absolute difference was 36·2 percentage points (95% CI 21·0 to 51·3; p<0·0001) for continuous rafutrombopag and 9·0 percentage points (-7·2 to 25·1; p=0·28) for switch rafutrombopag. In the safety set, adverse events occurred in 63 (90%) of 70 patients in the continuous group, 65 (92%) of 71 in the switch group, and 65 (93%) of 70 in the placebo group. Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 18 (26%), 26 (37%), and 22 (31%) patients, and serious adverse events in five (7%), eight (11%), and ten (14%), respectively. The most common adverse events were white blood cell count decreased (36 [51%], 38 [54%], and 44 [63%]), neutrophil count decreased (32 [46%], 44 [62%], and 44 [63%]), and anaemia (20 [29%], 25 [35%], and 16 [23%]) in the continuous, switch, and placebo groups, respectively. Liver enzyme-related adverse events occurred in 16 (23%), 13 (18%), and 18 (26%) patients. No fatal adverse events occurred during the double-blind treatment phase.
sections.conclusion: In patients with solid tumours and established chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia associated with platinum-based chemotherapy with an actual thrombocytopenia-related chemotherapy delay, continuous rafutrombopag improved the prespecified composite primary endpoint compared with placebo. The switch regimen did not show a significant difference from placebo. Safety findings should be interpreted in the context of cancer and ongoing chemotherapy.

items.title: Association of BMI with type 2 biomarkers, asthma burden, and severe asthma attack risk: an analysis of control groups of the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Obesity-related asthma is frequently described as a type 2-low phenotype, but data on type 2 biomarker distributions across BMI and their relationship with asthma attack risk are scarce. We aimed to examine the distribution of type 2 biomarkers across BMI categories in adolescents and adults with asthma and to investigate how BMI relates to risk of severe attacks.
sections.methods: We analysed data from the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis of control groups of 22 randomised placebo-controlled asthma trials, previously identified through a systematic review of MEDLINE from Jan 1, 1993, to April 1, 2021. We estimated annualised severe asthma attack rate ratios using negative binomial models, adjusted for sex, age, blood eosinophil count (BEC), fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), percent predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 s (ppFEV1), percent predicted forced vital capacity, treatment step, previous severe attacks, and trial.
sections.results: In the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis (n=6513), 2393 (37%) of 6513 participants with asthma had overweight (BMI 25 kg/m2 to <30 kg/m2) and 2723 (42%) had obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). Those with obesity had highest symptom burden, lowest baseline ppFEV1, and were most frequently on Global Initiative for Asthma step 5 treatment. Although the proportion of patients with dual type 2-high biomarkers (BEC ≥0·3 × 109 cells per L and FeNO ≥35 parts per billion) was lower in the obese versus normal BMI group (15% vs 26%; p<0·0001), the proportion of type 2-low asthma (BEC <0·15 × 109 cells per L and FeNO <20 ppb) was higher (18% vs 13%; p<0·0001), indicating that 82% of asthma patients with obesity still have some degree of type 2 inflammation. Compared with normal BMI, severe obesity (BMI ≥40 kg/m2) was associated with a significantly higher asthma attack risk (adjusted rate ratio 1·57, 95% CI 1·06-2·33).
sections.conclusion: Most patients with obesity-related asthma have evidence of type 2 inflammation despite a modest shift towards type 2-low disease. High BMI is associated with increased asthma burden and attack risk. These findings support a multidimensional view of obesity-associated asthma, in which type 2 inflammation frequently coexists with obesity-related mechanisms that independently contribute to disease burden and asthma attack risk.

items.title: Kinetics of myxovirus resistance protein A in adults with influenza and SARS-CoV-2 infection in the outpatient setting: a prospective study.

sections.objective: Respiratory viral infections have few virus-specific biomarkers, with current monitoring relying on subjective symptoms and non-specific biomarkers (procalcitonin and C-reactive protein). Myxovirus resistance protein A (MxA), a virus-specific biomarker, has shown rapid induction (1-2 h) and a moderate half-life (approximately 2·3 days) in experimental studies, but its protein-level kinetics remain poorly characterised in individuals with naturally acquired respiratory viral infections. We investigated MxA temporal kinetics in these patients, evaluated its potential as a biomarker for monitoring infection resolution, and assessed antiviral treatment efficacy in individuals with influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infection.
sections.methods: This single-centre, prospective cohort study enrolled adult outpatients (aged ≥18 years) with acute respiratory viral infections from the outpatient clinic at China-Japan Friendship Hospital in Beijing between Dec 11, 2023, and March 14, 2024, with 2-3 follow-up visits within 14 days. Patients were included if they presented with at least two respiratory symptoms with a symptom duration of seven days or less. Exclusion criteria included interferon therapy within 30 days, major surgery, myocardial infarction or stroke, substantial trauma or burns, vaccination within 30 days, or unavailable study samples. Viral pathogens included influenza, SARS-CoV-2, rhinovirus, human coronaviruses, respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and enterovirus. Peripheral blood samples were collected, and MxA levels were measured quantitatively using a fluorescence immunochromatography assay. Symptom severity, virological data, and antiviral treatment regimens were documented. Generalised estimating equation (GEE) models were used to assess the dynamic relationships between MxA levels, viral reads measured by multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing (mp-tNGS), and symptom severity, and the effects of antiviral treatments on MxA trajectories.
sections.results: A total of 201 outpatients with respiratory viral infections (59 influenza A, 43 influenza B, 78 SARS-CoV-2, 21 other viruses) with a median age of 34 years (41 for SARS-CoV-2) were included in this study. MxA levels were high on the day of symptom onset (median 116·0 ng/mL; IQR 84·7-166·0), peaked around day 2, and gradually decreased, falling below 50 ng/mL by day 10. SARS-CoV-2 showed significantly faster MxA decline than did influenza (p<0·0001). Multivariable GEE models showed that longitudinal changes in viral reads measured by mp-tNGS correlated positively and significantly with MxA levels (estimate=18·0; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10·4-25·7; p<0·0001). MxA correlated with mean total symptom scores (estimate=0·0029; 95% CI, 0·0018-0·0041; p<0·0001) and systemic symptom scores (estimate=0·0045; 95% CI, 0·0029-0·0060; p<0·0001), with strongest associations in the early infection phase. MxA levels also correlated positively with the mean respiratory symptom scores (estimate=0·0023; 95% CI, 0·0009-0·0038; p=0·0015). In individuals with influenza B, MxA levels declined significantly faster when treated with baloxavir compared with oseltamivir (estimate=-10·8; 95% CI, -17·1 to -4·5; p=0·0008). This faster decline trend aligned with changes observed in viral reads measured by mp-tNGS and clinical symptom improvement. In individuals with SARS-CoV-2, those receiving no antiviral therapy showed significantly slower MxA decline (p=0·022). Among patients with lower respiratory viral infections who experienced fever within 48 h of blood sampling (n=48), higher baseline MxA independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality (odds ratio 1·004; 95% CI, 1·001-1·008).
sections.conclusion: Our findings indicate that temporal changes in MxA levels correlate closely with viral load and symptom severity, suggesting that MxA could serve as a potential biomarker for monitoring infection resolution in respiratory viral infections. MxA decline is slower than viral load clearance (days 7-8), which may partially reflect its half-life; MxA levels generally fell below 50 ng/mL by day 10 after symptom onset, supporting its potential utility for monitoring infection resolution. Combining MxA with viral load testing provides a more comprehensive disease assessment. Additionally, MxA could help to guide antiviral management, although further validation is required. Limitations include small subgroup sample sizes, variable enrolment timing, low participant retention, and exclusion of immunosuppressed patients.

items.title: Seroreactivity and Heparin Exposure in Anti-Gal IgE Sensitized Patients Following Bioprosthetic Aortic Valve Replacement.

sections.objective: Patients may demonstrate asymptomatic seropositivity to galactose-α-1,3-galactose (alpha gal). Bioprosthetic valves contain significant alpha gal, and heparin may contain alpha gal. This manuscript seeks to characterize perioperative anti-gal immunoglobulin E (IgE) responses in patients undergoing surgical and transcatheter bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement. It will also evaluate heparin exposure in this population undergoing bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement.
sections.methods: This is a single-institution prospective cohort study. Anti-gal IgE levels were assessed preoperatively and at postoperative days 1 and 3 for transcatheter and surgical aortic valve recipients, respectively. Statistical analysis was completed using Wilcoxon's signed rank test.
sections.results: A total of 270 patients underwent preoperative testing for anti-gal and total IgE. Following an Institutional Review Board amendment, an additional postoperative sample was collected from 52 patients, of which 17 were seropositive. This equated to a prevalence of 32.7% (17/52). No patients demonstrated anaphylaxis, urticaria, or other symptoms indicative of an IgE-mediated response perioperatively. The median anti-gal IgE level preoperatively was 0.31 IU/mL (interquartile range [IQR]: 2.1 IU/mL), and the overall IgE level was 39.7 IU/mL (IQR: 153.8 IU/mL). Postoperatively, the median anti-gal IgE was 0.37 IU/mL (IQR: 2.1 IU/mL) (P = 0.22), and the median overall IgE was 56.1 IU/mL (IQR: 151.6 IU/mL) (P = 0.09).
sections.conclusion: The role of anti-gal IgE in long-term outcomes following bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement remains unclear. In addition, heparin use does appear to be safe perioperatively in this population in the absence of symptomatic alpha gal syndrome. These data suggest there is no statistically significant IgE-mediated response to alpha gal perioperatively following bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement.

items.title: Stopping versus continuing nebulised mucoactive therapy in people with cystic fibrosis established on elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (CF STORM): a multicentre, registry-based, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial.

sections.objective: Reducing treatment burden is a priority for people with cystic fibrosis and their families. Daily nebulised therapies are a substantial treatment burden. The CF STORM study aimed to assess whether cessation of daily nebulised mucoactive therapy (dornase alfa, hypertonic saline, or both) was non-inferior to continuing treatment in people with cystic fibrosis established on the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CTFR) modulator elexacaftor plus tezacaftor plus ivacaftor (ETI).
sections.methods: CF STORM was a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial, done across 40 adult or paediatric specialist cystic fibrosis centres in the UK. Eligible participants were aged 6 years or older with cystic fibrosis who were established on ETI treatment for at least 3 months, with a percentage predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) of at least 40%. Eligibility assessment, consent, randomisation, and data collection were all done within the UK Cystic Fibrosis Registry. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; using computer-generated random permuted blocks stratified by site and current mucoactive treatment) to stop their prescribed therapy (STOP) or continue their prescribed daily nebulised mucoactive therapy (dornase alfa, hypertonic saline, or both; CONTINUE). The primary outcome was change in ppFEV1 from baseline to 52 weeks (prespecified visit windows 51-55 weeks) assessed in all participants with primary outcome data. A non-inferiority margin of -3 percentage points was established for the difference between groups in ppFEV1. Safety was assessed in all randomly assigned participants who received at least one day of allocated treatment. This study is registered with the ISRCTN registry, ISRCTN14081521.
sections.results: Between July 8, 2021, and Aug 6, 2024, 1716 people were screened. Of 684 patients eligible for enrolment, 591 were randomly assigned to either the STOP group (n=297) or the CONTINUE group (n=294). Median age was 15·5 years (IQR 12·7-29·4) and mean baseline ppFEV1 was 89·4% (SD 18·2). Stopping mucoactive therapy was non-inferior to continuing treatment for change in ppFEV1 from baseline to 52 weeks in the primary analysis population (STOP n=195, CONTINUE n=195; unadjusted mean change 0·15 [SD 6·85] ppFEV1 in STOP vs -0·79 [SD 8·01] in CONTINUE; adjusted mean difference 0·97 percentage points, 95% CI -0·51 to 2·45). Pulmonary exacerbations were more frequent in the STOP group than the CONTINUE group (incidence 0·90 vs 0·67 per person-year; incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1·34, 95% CI 1·06 to 1·71), but no significant differences were identified between groups in pulmonary exacerbations leading to treatment with intravenous antibiotic therapy (incidence 0·12 vs 0·08 per person-year; IRR 1·55, 95% CI 0·78 to 3·08). No serious adverse reactions to dornase alfa or related serious adverse events associated with hypertonic saline were reported. One death, unrelated to the study intervention, occurred in the STOP group.
sections.conclusion: Stopping nebulised mucoactive therapy was non-inferior to continuing treatment. Registry-recorded pulmonary exacerbations were more common in the STOP group than the CONTINUE group. These data provide evidence that discontinuing nebulised mucoactive therapy is unlikely to result in worsening respiratory function for people with cystic fibrosis established on ETI aged 6 years and older with a baseline percent predicted FEV1 of at least 40%. A more cautious approach is recommended for people with ppFEV1 of 40-69%.

items.title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome.
items.abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour-stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

items.title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes.
items.abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3-7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self-non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer-promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

items.title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems.
items.abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR-Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools3-6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (PseCAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the PseCAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the PseCAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade-TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa PseCAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC-TnsB and TnsB-target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

items.title: A gut-brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila.
items.abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut-brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop-a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut-brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

items.title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals.
items.abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from -17cm (ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects-often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes-and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

items.title: Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids.
items.abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V-1 s-1 and submillimetre drift lengths-far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

items.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease.
items.abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb-seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

items.title: Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro.
items.abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1-7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

items.title: Middle-Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China.
items.abstract: Molecular and morphological evidence increasingly supports the view that most East Asian Middle to Late Pleistocene archaic Homo belong to Denisovans1, yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5-42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo, as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo.

items.title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST.
items.abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade-TniQ, TnsC and TnsA-TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

items.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains.
items.abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot-superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man's Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but lack topological protection3-5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man's Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6-8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man's Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

items.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage.
items.abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems-a centuries-old practice2,3-causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800-2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48-99) mW m-2-equivalent to 2.7 (1.8-3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing-originating from 0.4-0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52-110) mW m-2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (-9 (-15--2) mW m-2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

items.title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts.
items.abstract: Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1-4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999-2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species' elevational ranges: upper portions of species' ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

items.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation.
items.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease.

items.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing.
items.abstract: Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1-7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10-12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of O ( 1 ) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

items.title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway.
items.abstract: Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1-3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

items.title: An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals.
items.abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30-40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6.
