Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4-32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7-42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

items.title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP.
items.abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

items.title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis.
items.abstract: Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol-1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

items.title: Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study.

sections.objective: To assess whether prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children.
sections.methods: Population based cohort study. 3 643 376 children born in 2000-21 followed up for a median 9 years after birth in Sweden and 10 years in Norway and Denmark. Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period). Analyses were also done for monotherapy with methylphenidate, amphetamines, and atomoxetine. Unexposed pregnancies had no filled prescriptions for ADHD drugs during pregnancy.
sections.results: 7595 (0.2%) children were prenatally exposed to any ADHD drug (5230 methylphenidate, 1510 amphetamines, 553 atomoxetine only). About one third (n=2389) were exposed in the second/third trimester. After control for confounders, neither any nor second/third trimester exposure to ADHD drugs overall or by drug type was associated with increased risk of any neurodevelopmental disorder (weighted hazard ratio 1.05, 95% confidence interval 0.98 to 1.12), behavioural and emotional disorders (1.04, 0.97 to 1.12), or disorders of psychological and intellectual development (1.06, 0.96 to 1.18). Some elevated hazard ratios for infrequent outcomes were observed but not consistently identified across analyses.
sections.conclusion: This multinational cohort study found no increased risk of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders associated with prenatal exposure to ADHD drugs. These findings strengthen existing evidence and can assist pregnant people and clinicians in weighing the benefits and risks of such treatment during pregnancy.
sections.other: Nationwide register data on births, dispensed drugs, and specialist healthcare diagnoses from Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. Neurodevelopmental disorders (any, subgroups, and individual disorders), identified on the basis of inpatient and outpatient diagnoses in specialist healthcare. Propensity score overlap weighted Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted (weighted) hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Data from Denmark were analysed separately, and results were pooled using random effects meta-analysis.

items.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis.
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

items.title: Preconception antidepressant use in fathers and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring: Danish population based cohort study.

sections.objective: To investigate the associations between paternal antidepressant use during spermatogenesis and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring.
sections.methods: Nationwide population based cohort study. 1 365 887 liveborn singleton infants in Denmark from 2000 to 2023, followed from birth until 31 December 2023, death, emigration, or first occurrence of outcome, whichever came first.
sections.results: 23 572 (1.7%) offspring were born to fathers who used antidepressants during spermatogenesis. During a mean follow-up of 12.1 years (standard deviation 7.0 years), 18 353 (1.3%) offspring were diagnosed with a metabolic disorder, including 364 whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis and 17 989 whose fathers did not use antidepressants during this period (1.39 v 1.11 events per 1000 person years, respectively). Offspring whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis had a slightly higher risk of developing metabolic disorders (weighted hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04 to 1.38) compared with offspring who were unexposed. The associations varied by specific metabolic outcomes, with weighted hazard ratios ranging from 0.81 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.47) for hypercholesterolaemia to 1.64 (95% CI 1.21 to 2.22) for hypertension. However, when compared with offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during the pregnancy period only, no increased risk was found of any metabolic disorders (0.75, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.98) or of specific metabolic disorders.
sections.conclusion: The slightly increased risk of metabolic disorders in offspring of fathers using antidepressants during spermatogenesis was probably attributable to underlying paternal mental health disorders. These findings offer reassurance for men treated with antidepressants before pregnancy.
sections.other: Danish national registers. Metabolic disorders in offspring, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and overweight or obesity, were identified from hospital and prescription records. Offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during spermatogenesis (three months before pregnancy) were compared with those of fathers who did not take antidepressants during this period and fathers who used antidepressants only during pregnancy to further account for underlying paternal mental health conditions. Associations between paternal antidepressant use and metabolic disorders, collectively and individually, were estimated as propensity score weighted hazard ratios using Cox regression.

items.title: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells.
items.abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

items.title: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries: diagnostic pathways and stratified treatment.
items.abstract: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), formerly known as myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries, challenges the long-standing assumption that myocardial infarction is synonymous with obstructive coronary artery disease. Rather than a paradox, MINOCA reflects the limitations of angiography-centred paradigms and the complexity of contemporary cardiovascular pathophysiology. Consistent with this updated definition, this Review approaches MINOCA as a working diagnosis that encompasses diverse mechanisms, including plaque disruption, coronary vasomotor dysfunction, microvascular disease, and non-coronary conditions. We propose a pragmatic, mechanism-oriented framework for selecting and sequencing complementary investigations, highlighting how intracoronary imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, and coronary functional testing can be integrated according to the clinical scenario to refine diagnosis, while balancing diagnostic yield with procedural risk and resource availability. We discuss the implications for management, emphasising that treatment should be guided by underlying pathophysiology rather than a uniform approach derived from obstructive myocardial infarction. Emerging evidence supports the implementation of a stratified therapy to improve patient-centred outcomes. Finally, we discuss research priorities for improving mechanism-specific diagnosis and treatment, arguing that MINOCA represents both a conceptual advance and a transitional step toward a mechanism-based taxonomy of myocardial injury and infarction.

items.title: The blood-brain barrier imports diverse neuroprotective proteins through pathways impaired early in Alzheimer's disease models.
items.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) has been defined primarily by what it excludes, yet the scale and function of physiological blood-to-brain protein transport remain largely unknown. Using bioorthogonal proteomics, we find that the healthy BBB samples 191 plasma proteins and permits 92 into the brain parenchyma. Enriched for carrier and metabolic functions, these proteins home to distinct brain cell types, such as apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1) to astrocytes and alpha-1 antitrypsin (SERPINA1) to microglia. This cell-type tropism relies on a BBB-parenchyma receptor hand-off: APOA1 crosses the BBB via SR-B1 and engages astrocytic ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1), a key Alzheimer's risk gene, driving cholesterol efflux that supports synapse integrity. Unlike LPS-induced nonspecific leakage, early-stage 5xFAD mice show selective BBB transport remodeling, with reduced APOA1 and increased SERPINA1 uptake. Hepatic APOA1 overexpression restores APOA1 in the 5xFAD brain, rescuing astrocytic, synaptic, and behavioral deficits. These findings recast the BBB as a selective interface that recruits neuroprotective circulatory proteins for brain health.

items.title: TECR palmitoylation triggers a necrotic cell death program driving acute liver injury.
items.abstract: Acute liver injury caused by drug toxicity or immune activation remains a major clinical challenge with limited mechanistic understanding and few effective therapies. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized form of regulated cell death driven by palmitoylation of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident enzyme trans-2,3-enoyl-coenzyme A (CoA) reductase (TECR). We show that multi-site palmitoylation of TECR, redundantly catalyzed by the palmitoyl acyltransferases ZDHHC5 and ZDHHC2 and dynamically reversed by the depalmitoylase ABHD10, activates PERK-dependent ER stress signaling to trigger cell death. This cell death pathway is a TECR-dependent, palmitoylation-induced, ER stress-mediated necrotic cell death program (TPNCD). TPNCD contributes to liver injury in mouse models of acetaminophen- and concanavalin A-induced hepatotoxicity and is attenuated by hepatocyte-specific TECR ablation or by pharmacological inhibition of palmitoylation or ER stress signaling. Together, these findings establish TPNCD as a distinct, necrotic cell death pathway underlying acute liver injury and highlight new therapeutic entry points for hepatoprotection.

items.title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial.
items.abstract: We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.

items.title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula.
items.abstract: It has been unclear how Roman and later Germanic political control shaped the demography of Iberia and how it differed from other parts of Europe. We report genetic data from 243 ancient individuals dating to 100-800 CE, analyzed alongside 58 previously published individuals. In Roman times, we document an influx of people with ancestry from the Eastern Mediterranean and an influx of North Africans, especially in the center and south. Beginning in the 5th century, Germanic and Alan (Sarmatian) groups assumed political control. Although we identify individuals with Central-Northern European-associated ancestry, including siblings buried ∼725 km apart, the Hispano-Roman population remained continuous in Iberia. These demographic patterns contrast sharply with those in Britain, where major demographic change followed Rome's collapse, and with those in the central Mediterranean, where both periods were associated with profound transformations. Together, these findings highlight regional variation in admixture and continuity across post-Roman Europe.

items.title: In-cell discovery and characterization of a non-canonical bacterial protein translocation-folding complex.
items.abstract: Cryo-electron tomography has emerged as a powerful technology for in-cell structural biology and, in combination with breakthroughs in protein structure prediction, offers a unique opportunity for illuminating functions of previously uncharacterized macromolecular complexes. Here, we used the genome-reduced bacterium Mycoplasma pneumoniae as a minimal cell model and determined in-cell maps of an unknown complex located at the cell surface. By combining proteomics, structure prediction, integrative modeling, and bioinformatics, we identified the complex to include the conserved Sec-translocon and an extracellular dome-like structure largely formed by three uncharacterized proteins (Mdps). The Mdps show structural homology to the periplasmic ATP-independent foldase PrsA, with Mdp444 retaining key catalytic residues and activity. Our study provides the first sub-nanometer-resolution maps of the complete bacterial Sec-translocation machinery, depicting its association in SecA-mediated co-translational translocation and its coordination with an extracellular protein-folding system.

items.title: Single-cell visual proteomics of a minimal bacterium reveals structural coordination of gene expression machineries.
items.abstract: Translation is a central process in gene expression. Its regulation is complex, depends on factors that include cell state and the subcellular environment, and is subject to modulation via crosstalk to processes such as transcription or translocation. Here, we used cryo-electron tomography of native and antibiotic-perturbed Mycoplasma pneumoniae cells to resolve 140 maps that recapitulate bacterial translation during the initiation, elongation, and recycling phases. We visualized multiple transcription-translation complexes, allowing us to propose a threading-based translation reinitiation mechanism and to provide structural evidence for a long-hypothesized supercomplex that coordinates transcription, translation, and membrane attachment. We resolved abundant membrane-associated large ribosomal subunits and suggest that dissociation from membranes depends on the conditional initiation of new translation, consistent with a potentially conserved mechanism in mammalian cells. This work visualizes the multilayered control of bacterial translation and demonstrates the power of in-cell structural biology to investigate regulatory circuits in gene expression.

items.title: A pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition links APOE4 to cerebrovascular degeneration.
items.abstract: Cerebrovascular disease is a major but poorly understood feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD). The strongest genetic AD risk factor, apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4), is associated with cerebrovascular degeneration, including vascular amyloid deposition and fibrosis. To uncover how APOE4 promotes cerebrovascular pathology, we assembled a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human brain vasculature. In APOE4 carriers, pericyte abundance was significantly reduced and accompanied by the emergence of a myofibroblast-like cell population co-expressing contraction and extracellular matrix genes. Immunostaining confirmed non-vascular myofibroblasts in APOE4 human and mouse brains. We show that APOE4 pericytes transition into myofibroblasts that secrete fibronectin, which promotes vascular amyloid accumulation. Computational and experimental analyses identified elevated transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) signaling as the driver of this pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition. Inhibition of TGF-β restored pericyte coverage and reduced vascular fibrosis and amyloid to APOE3 levels, revealing a targetable mechanism linking APOE4 to cerebrovascular pathology in AD.

items.title: Shifts in embryonic oxygen levels cue heterochrony in limb initiation.
items.abstract: Heterochrony, or the alteration of developmental timing, is an important mechanism of evolutionary change. Avian species display synchronized growth of the forelimbs and hindlimbs, while mammalian species show delayed hindlimb development. We find that mammalian limb heterochrony is evident from the start of limb bud formation and is associated with heterochronic expression of T-box transcription factors. This heterochronic shift is not due to changes in cis-regulatory sequences controlling T-box gene expression but, unexpectedly, is dependent upon the differential oxygen levels to which avian and mammalian embryos are exposed prior to limb initiation. This is mediated, at least partially, by cRel, a transcription factor in the nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) family, and by the oxygen-sensing transcription factor hypoxia-inducible factor alpha (Hif1a). Together, these results provide a mechanistic understanding of an important example of developmental heterochrony and exemplify how the maternal environment can regulate timing during embryonic development.

items.title: CD4 T cells convert transient responses to KRAS inhibition to durable remissions in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is refractory to most therapies, including immunotherapies, for which reinvigoration of CD8 T cells through immune checkpoint blockade is insufficient to induce long-term, durable remissions. Direct KRAS inhibitors (KRASi) have shown clinical promise, although acquired resistance is common. We modeled KRASi response and relapse in mice and demonstrated that, unlike chemotherapy or combinations with checkpoint blockade, an interleukin (IL)-21 cytokine mimic (21h10) induced long-term, durable remissions. Its efficacy depends on T helper 1 (Th1)-polarized CD4 T cells, but not on CD8 T cells or tumor cell expression of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC class I). Specifically, CD4 T cells primed by type 2 conventional dendritic cells (cDC2s) produce interferon γ (IFN-γ), which promotes macrophage-mediated phagocytosis of tumor cells. Ex vivo treatment of human PDAC specimens with 21h10 induces IFN-γ production by infiltrating T cells. Thus, IL-21-elicited CD4 T cells exert antitumor activity in mice and potentially in humans, converting transient responses to KRAS inhibition into durable remissions.

items.title: Chloroplasts balance energy production and stress resilience via a cold-induced signaling pathway.
items.abstract: Chloroplasts are plant-specific organelles for photosynthesis and play crucial roles in stress response. However, how chloroplasts respond to cold stress remains unclear. Here, we identify an rapidly accelerated fifibrosarcoma (RAF)-like bi-kinase module, RAF3/6, as key mediators in chloroplast cold-stress responses. RAF3/6 separately localize to the cytoplasm and plasma membrane under growth conditions. Upon cold stress, RAF3/6 translocate into chloroplasts mediated by the chaperone HSP70-1, where they phosphorylate the PSII components D1 and LHCB1, promoting their redistribution across thylakoid membranes and subsequent degradation, thereby suppressing photosynthetic activity. Concurrently, RAF3/6 phosphorylate the chloroplast-to-nucleus shuttling protein WHY1, promoting its nuclear accumulation and cold-defense gene activation. Notably, the natural variation of RAF6 contains a latitude-correlated SNP that affects its chloroplast import, suggesting an evolutionary cold adaptation. Together, these findings reveal a cold-induced outside-in signaling pathway that links cytoplasmic cold perception to chloroplast remodeling and nuclear defense, establishing a conceptual framework that balances energy production with stress resilience.
keywords: balance of growth and stress adaptation

items.title: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery.
items.abstract: Over 150 modifications expand the RNA alphabet, yet all known natural modifications occur on nucleobases or ribose sugars, with none identified on the phosphate backbone. In contrast, phosphorothioates (PSs), in which a non-bridging phosphate oxygen is replaced with sulfur, are central to RNA therapeutics but have never been reliably detected in natural RNAs. Here, we develop sequencing- and mass spectrometry-based approaches to quantitatively map RNA PSs at single-nucleotide resolution. Across diverse archaeal species, we identify stereospecific PS modifications at rRNA and tRNA hotspots, which are dynamically regulated by sulfur availability and temperature. We uncover a diverse enzyme family that selectively modifies tRNA/rRNA substrates and whose evolutionary presence/absence matches the distribution of PSs. Enzyme loss causes inviability or temperature sensitivity, and functional analyses reveal that tRNA PSs enhance tRNA stability. These findings establish the first natural RNA phosphate-backbone modification and its enzymatic machinery, providing a foundation for mechanistic and functional exploration.

items.title: Single-cell-resolved genome atlas of prokaryoplankton inhabiting the ocean's interior.
items.abstract: The ocean's aphotic interior harbors three-quarters of planktonic bacteria and archaea (prokaryoplankton), whose composition, ecology, and biotechnological potential remain poorly constrained. To address this knowledge gap, we created Global Oceans Reference Genomes (GORG)-Dark, a dataset of 9,698 genomes from individual prokaryoplankton cells sampled unselectively across a broad range of depths, geographic locations, and environmental conditions below the ocean's photic surface. Biogeographic analyses revealed prokaryoplankton vertical stratification extending to abyssal depths, the presence of particle-attached lineages of Pelagibacterales, and the previously overlooked abundance of Patescibacteria and Nanoarchaeota in the Baltic and Black Seas. We identified coding potential for chemolithoautotrophy, pharmacologically relevant secondary metabolisms, and a distinct type of proteorhodopsins in prokaryoplankton lineages prevalent throughout the aphotic ocean. This study offers a quantitative, global assessment of the composition and coding potential of microorganisms inhabiting the vast ocean's interior and contributes an extensive, single-cell-resolved dataset to microbial oceanography's cyberinfrastructure.

items.title: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting triggers translational stress to promote viral replication.
items.abstract: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting (PRF) is a conserved viral strategy for expressing polyproteins from compact genomes. Although PRF is traditionally viewed as a structural mechanism, here we show that it functions as a regulatory signal that rewires host translation in favor of viral replication. A minimal SARS-CoV-2 PRF element is sufficient to activate the GCN2 arm of the integrated stress response (ISR) independently of the canonical ISR sensor ZAKα. This activation serves as a temporal switch during early infection to shut off host translation and is required for viral propagation in cells and human airway organoids. Proteomic and genetic screens identify DRG1 and IGF2BP3 as key mediators of PRF-induced GCN2 activation. We further show that this PRF-GCN2 axis is conserved in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-1 and West Nile virus, highlighting its broad relevance across RNA viruses. These findings reveal a sophisticated mechanism of viral translational control, highlighting PRF as a stress-inducing module that enhances viral replication.

items.title: Mitochondrial ATP promotes T cell differentiation through chromatin accessibility.
items.abstract: Immune elimination of chronic infection or cancer requires cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that adopt and maintain an effector phenotype. Cytotoxic T cell function is a bioenergetically demanding process. Here, we report the ability of D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) to act as a signaling molecule that increases mitochondrial ATP production and drives the conversion of proliferating T cells into cytotoxic effector cells. DAHB signaling switches ATP production from glycolysis to oxidative phosphorylation supported by fatty acid oxidation. This conversion elevates the level of a phosphagen, phosphocreatine (PCr). Both the PCr bioenergetic reserve and oxidative phosphorylation were required for T cell effector differentiation. DAHB-induced CD8 effector gene transcription was coupled to bioenergetics by BAF-complex-dependent remodeling of chromatin at effector loci. DAHB-enhanced CD8+ T cell antitumor activity both in vitro and in vivo. Together, these findings link cellular bioenergetics to the regulation of chromatin accessibility and gene expression required to support effector function.

items.title: Oxygen-responsive bacterial glycosphingolipid links symbiont fitness and immune development in neonatal host.
items.abstract: Symbiotic gut bacteria must re-establish themselves in every host generation, yet the molecular strategies enabling this inheritance remain poorly understood. Here, we show that Bacteroides fragilis uses a membrane glycolipid, alpha-galactosylceramide (BfaGC), to colonize the neonatal gut. Genome-wide fitness profiling revealed that BfaGC biosynthesis is selectively required during early life, when transient oxygenation creates a physiological bottleneck for strict anaerobes. Mechanistically, BfaGC reduces membrane proton permeability, sustaining the proton-motive force that supports aerobic respiration. This oxygen-responsive adaptation simultaneously generates a host-facing immunomodulatory signal that calibrates neonatal natural killer T (NKT) cell development, linking bacterial fitness to immune maturation through a single metabolite. The same mechanism also enables niche expansion by enterotoxigenic strains, revealing context-dependent consequences. Notably, this strategy is distinct among gut Bacteroidales: other prominent members synthesize a different sphingolipid subclass supporting broader fitness, implying divergent evolutionary strategies. Our findings provide time-resolved insight into how bacterial metabolites shape host-microbiota symbiosis across development.

items.title: The pitchfork sign in haemorrhagic type 2 choroidal neovascularisation: A comparative OCT study in eyes affected by inflammatory and non-inflammatory aetiologies.

sections.objective: To assess the prevalence and clinical implications of the "pitchfork sign" in a selected cohort of type 2 choroidal neovascularisation (T2 CNV) associated with retinal haemorrhage across maculopathies of different aetiologies.
sections.methods: This was a single-centre, retrospective study of 72 eyes from 68 patients with treatment-naive T2 CNV complicated by retinal haemorrhage. Aetiologies included myopic CNV (mCNV), exudative neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD), idiopathic CNV, inflammatory CNV, angioid streaks (AS) and pachychoroid disease spectrum complicated by CNVs. Multimodal imaging scans were collected at baseline and at 12-month follow-up. The prevalence and characteristics of the pitchfork sign were obtained across the groups. Functional and anatomical outcomes were recorded, beside number of injections provided.
sections.results: The pitchfork sign was identified in T2 CNV across all studied aetiologies, including mCNV (25.7%), AMD (42.9%), AS (20%), idiopathic (42.9%), inflammatory (66.7%), and pachychoroid disease (28.6%). BCVA significantly improved in mCNV (p = 0.0125), idiopathic (p = 0.0361), and pachychoroid groups (p = 0.0483) after treatment. SFCT was significantly greater in the idiopathic, inflammatory, and pachychoroid groups compared to the others (p < 0.001). The AMD group required a significantly higher number of anti-VEGF injections.
sections.conclusion: The pitchfork sign is not pathognomonic for inflammatory CNV, as it can also occur in non-inflammatory haemorrhagic T2 CNV, however a possible mechanical contribution of haemorrhage remains hypothesis-generating.

items.title: The Prognostic Value of PSMA-total Tumor Volume for Overall Survival in mHSPC: Exploratory Evaluation Within the ENZAMET Trial and PROMISE Registry.

sections.objective: ChemoHormonal Therapy Versus Androgen Ablation Randomized Trial for Extensive Disease in Prostate Cancer (CHAARTED) risk stratification is an important risk stratification tool in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). However, clinicians are increasingly using prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography (PSMA-PET)/computed tomography (CT). Here, the prognostic value of PSMA-total tumor volume (PSMA-TTV) for overall survival (OS) in a developmental cohort from the Enzalutamide in First-Line Androgen Deprivation Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer (ENZAMET) trial with validation in the larger Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) Registry was evaluated.
sections.methods: Participants who underwent PSMA-PET/CT before enrolment in the prospective phase 3 ENZAMET trial (development cohort) or were classified as having mHSPC in the ongoing international PROMISE Registry (validation cohort) were included, and PSMA-TTV was derived using a semiautomated method. In the ENZAMET dataset, the association of PSMA-TTV categories with time to progression and OS in addition to CHAARTED groups by conventional imaging, was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests. ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV categories were tested in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests and Cox regression analyses.
sections.results: Overall, 100 patients from ENZAMET and 993 patients from the PROMISE Registry were analyzed. The upper ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV category was ≥72 ml. In patients with CHAARTED criteria low-volume disease, 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml versus <72 ml was 36% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 16-83) versus 71% (60-85; p = 0.019) in survival curves; 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml was not associated with shorter OS in the ENZAMET subgroup (50% [32-78] vs 73% [63-85]; p = 0.063) but in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup (33% [27-40] vs 78% [75-81]; p < 0.001). The hazard ratio for upper PSMA-TTV category ≥72 ml was 6.8 (95% CI = 5.3-8.7) in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup.
sections.conclusion: PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml from an ENZAMET cohort is prognostic for OS in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort. Further validation of PSMA-TTV as a prognostic biomarker with potential to be a predictive marker to identify patients for intensification is warranted.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of variable perioperative antiplatelet regimens in patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy.

sections.objective: Current SVS recommendations for perioperative antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy (CEA) are limited. In acutely symptomatic patients, dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is recommended for secondary stroke prevention. In asymptomatic patients, there are no clear recommendations, though single antiplatelet therapy with aspirin (ASA) is commonly used. We examined the efficacy and safety of various perioperative antiplatelet regimens in patients who underwent CEA in the VQI.
sections.methods: We retrospectively reviewed all patients who underwent CEA in VQI from January 2003 to September 2024. We stratified patients based on their pre-operative antiplatelet regimen: No-antiplatelet, ASA-only, Clopidogrel-only, DAPT (ASA/Clopidogrel), and Alternative-DAPT (ASA/Alternative P2Y12 Inhibitors). We created propensity scores for each treatment regimen and assessed in-hospital stroke/death and bleeding complications using inverse probability of treatment weighted log binomial regression, with ASA-only as the reference group and adjusting for intraoperative protamine use and drain placement. We also assessed outcomes stratified by preoperative symptom status.
sections.results: Of 195,619 CEA patients: 53% received ASA-only, 11% No-antiplatelet, 6% Clopidogrel-only, 30% DAPT, and 1% Alternative-DAPT. The corresponding unadjusted rates of in-hospital stroke/death were 1.3%, 1.7%, 1.2%, 1.2%, and 1.6%. After adjustment, compared with ASA-only, in-hospital stroke/death was lower with Clopidogrel-only (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67-0.97) and DAPT (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.72-0.87). In symptomatic patients (26% of the cohort), there was a trend towards lower in-hospital stroke/death with DAPT (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.00). In asymptomatic patients, in-hospital stroke/death was lower with Clopidogrel-only (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52-0.90) and DAPT (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.64-0.83). Bleeding complications were higher with DAPT (RR 1.49, 95% CI 1.35-1.66) and trended toward higher with Clopidogrel-only (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.00-1.48) but were similar across other regimens.
sections.conclusion: Compared with ASA-monotherapy, Clopidogrel-monotherapy and DAPT were associated with lower rates of in-hospital stroke/death after CEA driven by lower rates of stroke, albeit with higher rates of bleeding complications, particularly with DAPT. These findings highlight Clopidogrel-monotherapy as a potential alternative to DAPT for patients undergoing CEA, with similar efficacy and more acceptable bleeding risk. Analyses in patients on alternative P2Y12 inhibitors were limited by sample size; however, analyses with a larger cohort will be valuable in the future. Overall, our findings emphasize a potential role for clopidogrel-monotherapy in stroke prevention among patients undergoing CEA and highlight the importance of individualized risk assessment.

items.title: Beyond injury grade: Anatomic location and outcomes after endovascular repair of blunt thoracic aortic injury.

sections.objective: Contemporary risk stratification for blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) has largely emphasized injury grade, whereas the prognostic importance of injury location remains poorly defined. More proximal injuries may require complex arch reconstruction and management of the supra-aortic branches, potentially increasing procedural risk. We evaluated the association between anatomic aortic injury zone and perioperative and long-term outcomes after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR).
sections.methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing TEVAR for BTAI in the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative from 2013 through April 1, 2026. Patients were classified according to the proximal extent of the aortic injury as proximal (zones 0-2), isthmic (zone 3), or distal (zones 4-5). Multinomial propensity scores incorporating pretreatment demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, and injury-severity variables were used to generate stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights. Weighted logistic regression with center-clustered standard errors evaluated perioperative outcomes. Cox regression evaluated all-cause mortality, and Fine-Gray regression evaluated aorta- or branch-related reintervention with death treated as a competing event. Zone 3 served as the reference group.
sections.results: Among 2,693 patients, 551 (20.5%) had proximal injuries, 1,772 (65.8%) had zone 3 injuries, and 370 (13.7%) had distal injuries. Injury-grade distributions did not differ significantly among groups. After weighting, proximal injury was associated with greater in-hospital mortality compared with zone 3 injury (11.0% vs. 8.5%; odds ratio [OR], 1.33; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.76; P=0.046) and greater 30-day aortic reintervention (2.2% vs. 0.8%; OR, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.30-6.92; P=0.010). Stroke and spinal cord ischemia did not differ significantly. Proximal injury was also associated with a greater cumulative incidence of aortic reintervention (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.06-3.53; P=0.031), although its association with all-cause mortality during follow-up did not reach statistical significance (hazard ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.99-1.65; P=0.060). Distal injury was not associated with increased perioperative or long-term adverse outcomes compared with zone 3 injury.
sections.conclusion: Among patients undergoing TEVAR for BTAI, proximal injury location was associated with greater in-hospital mortality and aortic reintervention despite similar injury-grade distributions. Anatomic injury zone may complement injury grade when assessing procedural risk and planning postoperative surveillance.

items.title: Epigenetic Aging and Severity of Nocturnal Intermittent Hypoxia.

sections.objective: Nocturnal intermittent hypoxia (IH) is a hallmark feature of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and contributes to oxidative stress and inflammation, which in turn may accelerate biological aging. Epigenetic clocks can estimate biological age from DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns.
sections.methods: We studied adults referred for suspected OSA in a multisite sleep and circadian research network, a cross-sectional observational cohort (2016-2021). IH severity was assessed using the 4% oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from home sleep apnea testing or in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG). DNAm from peripheral blood leukocytes was assayed using Illumina EPIC arrays. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and pace of aging were calculated using multiple DNAm clocks. Linear regression models were adjusted for leukocyte composition, age, sex, ethnicity, BMI, smoking, site, alcohol, diabetes, and hypertension. A false discovery rate of 0.05 was used.
sections.results: A total of 1364 participants were included (median age, 56 yrs; median ODI, 16/h; median BMI, 32 kg/m2; 57% male). Higher ODI was associated with EAA for PhenoAge (β = 0.028, adjusted P = .0048) and with pace of aging (DunedinPACE, β = 0.0005, adjusted P =.0012). No significant associations were observed for first-generation clocks.
sections.conclusion: Greater IH severity, as assessed by ODI, was independently associated with increased biological aging as measured by PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clocks. These findings support a link between OSA and biological aging, raising the possibility of using epigenetic age measures as biomarkers of OSA-related morbidity.
sections.other: Is greater severity of IH associated with increased biological aging?

items.title: DHEA-S in Pulmonary Hypertension: Insights from PVDOMICS.

sections.objective: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) associates with disease severity in pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, prior studies focused on Group 1 disease; it is unknown whether DHEA-S associates with PH severity in other etiologies. It also remains unclear if DHEA-S associations with PH severity differ by sex or menopausal status.
sections.methods: We analyzed data from PVDOMICS, including 85 healthy controls and 710 participants with PH. Venous plasma DHEA-S levels were measured by ultraperformance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations between DHEA-S levels and invasive hemodynamics, right ventricular (RV) systolic function, and six-minute walk distance (6MWD). Analyses were stratified by sex and WSPH group, with exploratory stratification by menopausal status among subjects with Group 1 PH.
sections.results: DHEA-S levels were lower in all WSPH Groups compared with controls (adjusted p<0.01 for all). Associations between DHEA-S levels and PH severity metrics appeared most prominent in females with Group 1 PH. A doubling of DHEA-S was associated with a 2.8 mmHg (95% CI 1.6-4.1) lower mean pulmonary artery pressure, 3.2% (95% CI 2.0-4.4%) higher RV ejection fraction, and 22m (95% CI 11-33) farther 6MWD (all p<0.01). Higher DHEA-S associated with better RV function, but not pulmonary hemodynamics or 6MWD in females with Group 2 PH and males with Group 3 PH. In Group 1 PH, associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity appeared stronger in post-menopausal compared with premenopausal females.
sections.conclusion: Lower DHEA-S is a consistent feature across PH etiologies, but its association with disease severity appeared most pronounced in females with Group 1 PH. Modulation of DHEA-S levels or the pathways governing its regulation may represent a therapeutic target in PH, warranting further mechanistic study.
sections.other: Do associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity differ by PH etiology, sex, or menopausal status?

items.title: Is Remote Ischemic Preconditioning Effective for Improving Claudication in Peripheral Artery Disease? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

sections.objective: To perform a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the efficacy of remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) in improving claudication in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) compared with placebo or no intervention.
sections.methods: We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases through June 24, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing RIPC with placebo or no intervention in patients with PAD, defined by an ankle-brachial index (ABI) ≤ 0.90 in association with clinical intermittent claudication (IC), up to Rutherford III or Fontaine IIB. The primary outcomes were changes from baseline in intermittent claudication distance (ICD) and maximum walking distance (MWD).
sections.results: Six RCTs including 240 patients met the inclusion criteria; 122 patients (50.8%) received RIPC, whereas 118 patients (49.2%) received placebo or no intervention. RIPC was associated with greater changes from baseline in both ICD (MD 15.16 meters; 95% CI 8.65 to 21.68; P < 0.00001; I2=0%) and MWD (MD 20.90 meters; 95% CI 10.65 to 31.15; P < 0.0001; I2=0%). In the subgroup analysis including only trials using extended 28-day RIPC protocols, RIPC was also associated with significant improvements in ICD (MD 18.36 meters; 95% CI 1.33 to 35.39; P=0.03; I2=11%) and MWD (MD 20.88 meters; 95% CI 10.58 to 31.18; P < 0.0001; I2=0%).
sections.conclusion: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, RIPC was effective in improving claudication symptoms in patients with PAD. However, further clinical trials with well-established protocols and adequately powered sample sizes are needed before the routine clinical application of RIPC can be supported.

items.title: Combined Iliac Vein Stenting and Lymphaticovenular Anastomosis for Post-Oncological Lower Extremity Lymphedema with Iliac Vein Compression Syndrome: Longitudinal Volume Reduction and Time-Dependent Predictors.

sections.objective: To evaluate the longitudinal trajectory of limb volume reduction following combined iliac vein stenting and lymphaticovenular anastomosis (LVA) in patients with post-oncological lower extremity lymphedema and concurrent iliac vein compression syndrome (IVCS), and to identify time-dependent predictors of volumetric response.
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort study included 122 patients with post-oncological lower extremity lymphedema and IVCS (>50% iliac vein stenosis) treated from June 2018 to June 2023. Patients underwent staged iliac vein stenting and LVA, either stenting-first or in reverse sequence. The primary outcome was volume reduction rate (VRR) at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Secondary outcomes were Lymphedema Quality of Life (LYMQoL) scores and complications.
sections.results: Mean limb volume decreased from 10302.9 mL at baseline to 8247.9 mL at 24 months (P < 0.001). VRR increased from 10.7% at 1 month to 19.7% at 12 months, plateauing thereafter (12 vs. 24 months: P = 0.995). Over 92% of improvement occurred within 6 months. Multivariable regression identified lymphedema stage (β = -5.51, P < 0.001) and iliac vein stenosis severity (β = 1.39, P = 0.012) as independent predictors at 1 and 3 months. Body mass index was the sole predictor at 6 months (β = 0.35, P = 0.010). No predictors were identified at 12 or 24 months. Stenting-first sequence yielded higher VRR at 1, 3, and 6 months (all P ≤ 0.001), with convergence thereafter. All LYMQoL domains improved significantly (all P < 0.001). Complication rates were low with no procedure-related mortality.
sections.conclusion: Combined iliac vein stenting and LVA achieves sustained limb volume reduction in post-oncological lymphedema with IVCS. Lymphedema stage, stenosis severity, and body mass index are time-dependent predictors. Stenting-first sequence accelerates early recovery without compromising long-term outcomes.

items.title: Triamcinolone Acetonide for Upper Eyelid Retraction in Thyroid Eye Disease: A Systematic Review and Single-Arm Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Upper eyelid retraction is the most frequent sign of thyroid eye disease, yet surgical correction is deferred until the disease is quiescent, and systemic corticosteroids and targeted biologics carry appreciable toxicity and cost. We searched 4 databases to April, 2026, and pooled 12 studies (540 patients, 741 analytical units) evaluating local periocular triamcinolone acetonide injection, extracting only the triamcinolone arm of comparative trials. Injection lowered margin reflex distance-1 by a mean of 1.78 mm (95% CI, 1.20 to 2.35 mm) and produced clinical improvement in 87.0% of treated units (95% CI, 80.0% to 93.0%). Clinical activity score and proptosis did not change significantly. Transient ocular hypertension occurred in 4.0% and post-injection ptosis in 0.6% (95% CI, 0.2% to 2.0% by generalized linear mixed model). Certainty of evidence was very low to low throughout because all data derive from uncontrolled single-arm cohorts. Local triamcinolone injection is an inexpensive, accessible option for eyelid retraction during active disease, although controlled trials are lacking.

items.title: Residual Calcium Density Reflects Plaque Vulnerability and Cerebrovascular Event Risk in Symptomatic Carotid Disease.

sections.objective: The relationship between carotid calcification characteristics and plaque vulnerability or rupture risk remains controversial. This study investigated whether quantitative computed tomography angiography (CTA) metrics of carotid calcification (calcium score, volume, density, and residual [volume normalised] calcium density) are associated with plaque vulnerability, symptomatic status, and recurrent ipsilateral ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA) in patients with carotid artery disease ipsilateral to cerebrovascular symptoms.
sections.methods: Patients with recent TIA or ischaemic stroke and ipsilateral ≥ 2 mm carotid plaque with < 70% stenosis underwent baseline CTA and magnetic resonance imaging. Calcifications on CTA (≥ 130 HU) were segmented, yielding calcium score, volume, and density. As volume and density are strongly correlated, volume normalised residual calcium density was calculated as standardised residuals from a density-volume regression model. Associations with vulnerable plaque features (intraplaque haemorrhage, thin or ruptured fibrous cap, lipid rich necrotic core, and ulceration), symptomatic side, and recurrent ipsilateral TIA or ischaemic stroke were assessed using logistic, conditional logistic, and Cox regression models.
sections.results: Among 193 patients (mean age 67.8 ± 8.5 years, 74.6% men), 26 had recurrent ipsilateral TIA (n = 14) or ischaemic stroke (n = 12), over median five year follow up. Lower calcium density and residual calcium density were independently associated with vulnerable plaque features (odds ratios [ORs] 0.40 - 0.60). Residual calcium density was independently associated with symptomatic side (OR 0.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.47 - 0.88) and recurrent TIA or ischaemic stroke (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 - 0.95).
sections.conclusion: Residual calcium density is an independent marker of carotid plaque vulnerability and ipsilateral ischaemic stroke and TIA risk in patients with carotid artery disease ipsilateral to cerebrovascular symptoms.

items.title: Wider social determinants of the presentation and outcomes of patients enrolled in small abdominal aortic aneurysm surveillance.

sections.objective: Elective repair offers better outcomes than urgent repair for patients in small abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) surveillance who reach treatment thresholds, or treatment being declined due to surgical risk. Internationally, socioeconomically deprived, ethnic minority, and rural populations receive fewer guideline recommended surgical procedures. In Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), Māori face barriers to timely surgical access. This multicentre, observational analysis of prospectively collected AAA surveillance data (2002 - 2019) examined disparities in AAA stage at diagnosis and elective repair by socioeconomic deprivation, ethnicity, and distance to vascular services.
sections.methods: Patients with incidentally detected AAAs were grouped by socioeconomic deprivation, ethnicity (Māori/non-Māori), and travel time to vascular services. Outcomes included age and AAA diameter at diagnosis, and elective repair rates. Cumulative incidence functions estimated 36 month probability of elective repair, with cause specific Cox regression adjusted for comorbidities.
sections.results: 1 684 patients were eligible for analysis. Patients in highly deprived areas were diagnosed younger, but higher deprivation was associated with lower elective repair rates (hazard ratio [HR] 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.98; p = .02). Māori were diagnosed younger (68.7 vs. 73.4 years; p < .001) yet had lower elective repair rates for medium (≥ 45 mm) AAAs in univariable analysis (36 month probability 0.27 vs. 0.54; p = .04) and multivariable analysis controlling for covariates (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29 - 0.86; p = .01) despite reaching treatment thresholds at least as often. Rural location was not associated with repair rates.
sections.conclusion: Socioeconomic and ethnic inequities in outcomes of small AAA surveillance exist in NZ. Patients in more deprived areas had lower elective repair rates. Māori received fewer elective repairs despite equivalent or greater clinical need, likely reflecting higher comorbidity burden and operative risk. Earlier diagnosis, improved access to specialist care, including national AAA screening, enhanced risk factor management, and strengthened primary care access may reduce inequity. Socioeconomic, ethnic, and geographical factors should inform equitable screening and service delivery.

items.title: From Bladder to Aorta: Mycobacterium bovis Endograft Infection Following Intravesical BCG Therapy.
items.abstract: Mycobacterium bovis is an uncommon cause of human tuberculosis, arising most often in clinical practice as a complication of intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) therapy for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer. Systemic spread is rare but well documented, and carries the potential for serious extra-urinary sequelae, including prosthetic vascular infection. We report the case of a 79-year-old man who developed M. bovis infection of a fenestrated endovascular aortic graft with history of intravesical BCG therapy. He came to attention with a prolonged history of constitutional decline, and was ultimately found to harbour enlarging para-aortic collections in close relation to the graft. Reaching a diagnosis demanded advanced imaging and targeted microbiological investigation, including molecular testing of aspirated material. Treatment comprised endovascular relining, image-guided drainage, and an extended course of anti-tuberculous therapy. The case draws attention to a rare but important diagnostic pitfall, and to the difficulties that arise when prosthetic infection cannot be managed surgically.

items.title: Trends in Self-Reported Vision Difficulty and Eye Care Utilization Among Adults With Diabetes.

sections.objective: Adults with diabetes are at high risk for diabetic eye diseases and recommended to receive regular screening. To examine national trends in prevalence of vision difficulty and eye care utilization among US adults with diabetes from 1997 to 2024.
sections.methods: Cross-sectional trend analysis of National Health Interview Survey data from US adults aged 18 years or older with diabetes.
sections.results: The full sample included 74 719 individuals. Prevalence of vision difficulty declined between 1997 (23.8%) and 2006 (17.1%; average percent change [APC], -3.4%; 95% CI, -8.8% to -1.6%), followed by no change through 2024. Prevalence of eye care utilization increased only between 2014 (50.3%) and 2018 (55.3%; APC, 3.0%; 95% CI, 0.1% to 8.4%).
sections.conclusion: Over nearly 3 decades in the US, prevalence of vision difficulty among adults with diabetes initially declined and then plateaued, and prevalence of eye care utilization increased modestly. Findings highlight opportunities to support vision health in this high-risk population.
sections.other: Age, sex, race and ethnicity, education, seeing an eye care practitioner in the past year, current insulin use, diabetes type, time since diabetes diagnoses, and health insurance coverage. The primary outcomes examined were self-reported vision loss and eye care utilization. Based on the survey questions assessing vision loss, it was not possible to determine whether reported vision loss was central, peripheral, or both, or whether it was specific to 1 eye or both. Analyses examined annual prevalence and trends from 1997 to 2018 and 2019 to 2024.

items.title: Complications From Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ZEDS Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO) is a well-recognized cause of many complications that may lead to loss of vision. To determine how treatment with oral valacyclovir, 1000 mg, daily for 12 months was associated with the development of complications from HZO up to 18 months following study enrollment.
sections.methods: The Zoster Eye Disease Study (ZEDS) was a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 95 sites from November 2017 to June 2024. Participants had a history of HZO rash at any time and documented keratitis or iritis within 1 year. This post hoc analysis was conducted among all 527 original participants from September 2024 to July 2026. Participants were randomized to valacyclovir, 1000 mg, daily or placebo for 12 months and monitored every 3 months for 18 months.
sections.results: Of 261 and 266 participants randomized to placebo or valacyclovir, respectively, 240 (92.0%) and 250 (94.0%) completed treatment through 12 months and 233 (89.3%) and 247 (92.9%) through 18 months. New complications among those randomized to placebo and valacyclovir, respectively, were: corneal scarring (12 months: 58 [40.6%] vs 54 [38.6%]; difference, 2.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -9.4 to 13.4; P = .83; 18 months: 64 [44.8%] vs 67 [47.9%]; difference, -3.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -14.7 to 8.5; P = .69), corneal neovascularization (12 months: 15 [6.3%] vs 14 [5.7%]; difference, 0.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.61 to 4.8; P = .93; 18 months: 20 [8.4%] vs 20 [8.1%]; difference, 0.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.6 to 5.2; P > .99), neurotrophic keratopathy at 12 months (16/234 [6.8%] vs 16/243 [6.6%]; difference, 0.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.2 to 4.8; P > .99) or 18 months (22/234 [9.4%] vs 19/243 [7.8%]; difference, 1.6 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.5 to 6.6; P = .65), cataract (12 months: 28 [18.9%] vs 27 [17.2%]; difference, 1.7 percentage points; 95% CI, -6.9 to 10.4; P = .70; 18 months: 31 [20.9%] vs 34 [21.7%]; difference, -0.7 percentage points; 95% CI, -9.9 to 8.5; P = .88), and worsening cataract (12 months: 18 [12.8%]vs 16 [11.8%]; difference, 1.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -6.7 to 8.7; P = .80; 18 months: 20 [13.9%] vs 21 [14.7%]; difference, -0.80 percentage points; 95% CI, -8.9 to 7.3; P = .85).
sections.conclusion: In this post hoc analysis of a randomized clinical trial, no differences in complications through 18 months were suggested following 12 months of valacyclovir treatment in individuals with HZO and prior keratitis or iritis. The analysis found no evidence that suppressive valacyclovir reduced longer-term complications; however, the study was not designed or powered to detect differences in complication rates.
sections.other: ZEDS was designed to test whether a suppressive dose of valacyclovir delayed the onset of new or worsening keratitis or iritis due to HZO. The present study involved post hoc analyses of prespecified ocular and systemic complications that were not primary end points.

items.title: Process, Heterogeneity, and Modifiable Risk Factors of Postoperative Recovery After Cardiac Surgery.

sections.objective: Cardiac surgery improves clinical endpoints but imposes challenges in recovery. Understanding patient-reported postoperative recovery is crucial for optimal care. The goal of this study was to reveal the process, heterogeneity, and modifiable risk factors of patient-reported postoperative recovery.
sections.methods: In this multicenter prospective cohort study involving patients undergoing nonemergent cardiac surgery, patient-reported outcomes were assessed using the Fuwai-Cardiac Recovery Scale (a 9-item scale including symptoms and functional status) at baseline and 8 timepoints after surgery (days 1-4, weeks 2 and 3, and months 1 and 3). Total score and each item score of the Fuwai-Cardiac Recovery Scale were reported to characterize the recovery process. Group-based trajectory models were applied to detect heterogeneity, and trajectory with the largest area under trajectory curve was defined as poor recovery pattern. Multivariable stepwise regression was performed to uncover modifiable risk factors of poor recovery.
sections.results: From May 2023 to December 2024, 2,993 patients from 8 Chinese centers were enrolled. The proportions of patients achieving a total score ≤30 (less likely to experience 3-month unplanned readmission) were 77.4% at discharge (week 2) and 97.7% at month 3. Areas under the curve of the item score within 2 weeks, ranked from highest to lowest, were thirst, toileting dependency, poor mobility, fatigue, pain, poor sleep, poor appetite, shortness of breath, and nausea or vomiting. Three different poor recovery patterns were identified: 1) "initial worsening followed by improving" in shortness of breath, poor appetite, nausea or vomiting, poor sleep, and pain; 2) "persistently not improving" in thirst; and 3) "slowly improving" in fatigue, poor mobility, and toileting dependency. Several modifiable risk factors were significantly associated with poor recovery patterns, including smoking (shortness of breath, OR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.07-2.24), obesity (poor mobility, OR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.02-2.26), and anemia (poor appetite, OR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.11-1.95; fatigue, OR: 1.36; 95% CI: 1.11-1.67).
sections.conclusion: Recovery after cardiac surgery is a dynamic trajectory that unfolds over time, differs substantially among patients, and offers opportunities for earlier recognition and intervention.

items.title: A consensus spinal cord cell-type atlas across mouse, macaque, and human.
items.abstract: The spinal cord contains cell types critical for motor, sensory, and autonomic function, many of which are implicated in neurological disease and injury. Yet no shared molecular framework links human spinal cord cell types to the animal models used to study them. Here, we present a cross-species atlas integrating single-nucleus gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomics from over one million nuclei spanning cervical to sacral segments in human, macaque, and mouse. Consensus clustering resolves 111 cell type groups replicable across all three species, whose spatial distributions map spinal laminae and nuclei, including Clarke's column. Identity and laminar organization are highly conserved, yet abundance and expression are allometrically scaled, with the dorsal horn being the principal site of divergence, concentrated in neurotransmitter receptor genes and including a primate-specific glycine receptor subunit switch. Sequence models uncover a conserved transcription factor grammar and nominate motifs underlying enhancer-adeno-associated virus (AAV) access to a divergent dorsal horn population.

items.title: Toward a shared infrastructure for preclinical discovery: Why animal model tissue and biofluid biobanks are needed.
items.abstract: Animal model tissues and biofluids are indispensable yet underused assets in preclinical research. We argue that standardized, shareable biobanks could reduce duplication, improve technical reproducibility, strengthen biomarker translation, lower animal use, and create scalable infrastructures for academia and industry.

items.title: Temporal changes in metabolism guide oligodendrocyte precursor cell dynamics in aging and multiple sclerosis.
items.abstract: Impaired oligodendrocyte precursor cell (OPC) differentiation limits myelin renewal in aging and contributes to multiple sclerosis (MS) progression. How aging drives OPC deficits remains incompletely understood. We find dysregulation of genes associated with the circadian clock, including Bmal1, and metabolism in aged compared with young OPCs. Targeted loss of Bmal1 in OPCs drives metabolic dysfunction, leading to cellular senescence and impaired dynamics. OPC proliferation and differentiation occur at different rates throughout the day in young adult mice and become disrupted with aging. Chronotherapeutic targeting of BMAL1-controlled sirtuin signaling restores Bmal1-disrupted OPC dynamics after demyelination via sirtuin 2 (Sirt2)-dependent mechanisms. Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived OPCs from MS patients and MS lesion oligodendroglia recapitulate BMAL1 and SIRT2 disruptions. These findings establish BMAL1 as a key regulator of OPC energy metabolism, sirtuin homeostasis, and senescence. We anticipate that this work will provide a foundation for future studies investigating the interconnected roles of aging, circadian disruption, and myelin biology.

items.title: Optogenetic mimicry of drug action: Tools and models to dissect the dopamine-dependent core of addiction.
items.abstract: Drug addiction is characterized by compulsive drug use despite negative consequences, reflecting maladaptive changes in brain circuits. Elucidating the underlying neural mechanisms relies on animal models that capture core features of the disorder. Here, we review optogenetic mimicry mouse models that leverage a defining core of addictive drugs-their ability to elevate mesolimbic dopamine. Analogous to gold-standard pharmacological self-administration paradigms, these models allow animals to self-induce dopamine transients either directly, via optogenetic activation of ventral tegmental area dopamine neurons, or indirectly, via optogenetic inhibition of midbrain GABA interneurons. Both protocols are robustly reinforcing and induce lasting behavioral and synaptic adaptations. We compare these adaptations with those observed in established rodent models of psychostimulant and opioid addiction. We argue that optogenetic mimicry of drug-evoked mesolimbic dopamine transients recapitulates key features of addiction while uniquely enabling cell-type- and circuit-specific mechanistic investigations of reinforcement and maladaptive plasticity.

items.title: Sparse component analysis: A method that uncovers separable computations within neural population activity.
items.abstract: In many neural populations, the computationally relevant signals are posited to be a set of "latent factors"-signals shared across many individual neurons. A given brain area may perform many computations, each associated with distinct factors, which can together compose an overall action. The methods for uncovering such structure typically require supervision, which can limit the discovery of novel aspects of activity. Here, we introduce sparse component analysis (SCA), an unsupervised approach. SCA facilitated surprisingly clear parcellations of neural activity across a range of behaviors, when seeking both linear and nonlinear embeddings. We applied SCA to motor cortex activity from reaching and cycling monkeys, single-trial imaging data from C. elegans, and activity from a multitask artificial network. SCA revealed both simple and unexpected instances where the overall population response was built compositionally from sets of factors with distinct computational roles.

items.title: Effect of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg on glycaemic outcomes and their association with weight loss: a substudy of the randomised, double-masked, parallel-group, phase 3a REDEFINE 2 trial.

sections.objective: CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg, a fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide, demonstrated substantial weight loss versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes in REDEFINE 2. We aimed to evaluate glycaemic outcomes in a subgroup of participants who underwent continuous glucose monitoring (CGM).
sections.methods: REDEFINE 2 was a global 68-week, double-masked, parallel-group phase 3a trial that included 1206 adults from 12 countries with a BMI of at least 27 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes who were randomly assigned (3:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg or placebo. Participants were assigned treatment using a centralised web-based system. Participants, investigators, site staff, and the sponsor were masked to group allocation throughout the trial. A subgroup of 199 participants from 35 US sites (including university hospitals, health-care centres, research centres, and other centres) were equipped with a CGM device (Dexcom G6 Pro) for double-masked measurements from week -3 to 0, week 20 to 24, and week 64 to 68. Prespecified secondary endpoints included change in time in range (TIR; 3·9-10·0 mmol/L) and change in time in tight range (TITR; 3·9-7·8 mmol/L) for CagriSema versus placebo. REDEFINE 2 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05394519, and is completed.
sections.results: Between Feb 1 and Aug 11, 2023, 199 participants were enrolled in the CGM subgroup (149 in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and 50 in the placebo group) and had their CGM data analysed. The mean age of participants in the CGM subgroup was 60·4 years (SD 11·3), 106 (53%) of the 199 participants were female, 93 (47%) were male, and 160 (80%) were White. Compared with placebo, participants in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group had a significant increase from baseline to week 68 in mean percentage of TIR (45·9 percentage points [SE 1·2] vs 3·0 percentage points [5·7]; estimated treatment difference [ETD] 42·9 percentage points [95% CI 30·7-55·0]; p<0·0001) and mean percentage of TITR (50·4 percentage points [2·2] vs 2·8 percentage points [2·7]; ETD 47·7 percentage points [95% CI 40·7-54·7]; p<0·0001) using the trial product estimand. The overall observed mean change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68 was -16·7% (SD 7·9) for the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and -1·8% (4·5) for the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 144 (97%) of 149 participants in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and in 42 (84%) of 50 participants in the placebo group, and were predominantly mild or moderate in severity.
sections.conclusion: In this hypothesis-generating analysis, CGM-based assessments provided evidence of an effect of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg on glycaemic outcomes in people living with type 2 diabetes. These findings support the potential use of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg for improving glucose control in people living with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: The global hypertension care cascade in May Measurement Month 2023: a cross-sectional opportunistic blood pressure screening campaign.

sections.objective: Raised blood pressure is the leading contributor to global morbidity and mortality. May Measurement Month is an annual global blood pressure screening campaign aimed at raising hypertension awareness. In this study we present the results of the 2023 campaign.
sections.methods: In this multinational, cross-sectional blood pressure screening survey, volunteers aged 18 years and older were opportunistically recruited using convenience sampling. Recruitment took place between May 1 and July 31, 2023, at screening sites (eg, hospitals, community centres, etc) across 70 countries. Participants completed three sitting blood pressure measurements and a questionnaire on demographic, clinical, and lifestyle information all on the day of recruitment. Raised blood pressure was defined as systolic blood pressure of 140 mm Hg or more or diastolic blood pressure of 90 mm Hg or more or both (ie, from an average of the mean of the second and third of three readings). Hypertension was defined as raised blood pressure, taking blood pressure-lowering medication, or a combination of the two. The main outcome was to describe the hypertension care cascade at the global and regional level and by sex.
sections.results: Of 673 304 participants screened (mean age 47·5 years [SD 17·3]; 362 116 [54·2%] were female and 306 241 [45·5%] were male), 547 584 (81·3%) were from lower-income or middle-income countries and 95 920 (14·2%) had never previously had their blood pressure measured. Of 258 802 participants with hypertension (121 168 [39·6%] were male and 135 242 [37·3%] were female), 163 295 (63·1%) were aware, 156 218 (60·4%) were being treated, 89 530 (34·6%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 140/90 mm Hg, and 40 748 (15·7%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 130/80 mm Hg. Awareness, treatment, and control rates were all higher among females than males. Of 156 218 taking blood pressure-lowering medication, 89 530 (57·3%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 140/90 mm Hg and 40 748 (26·1%) to lower than 130/80 mm Hg, with 67 062 (51·6%) using monotherapy. 169 272 participants had untreated or inadequately treated hypertension (25·1% of those surveyed; 65·4% of participants with hypertension). 128 448 (44·8%) of those with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or higher, 35 482 (68·8%) with a history of diabetes, 5041 (68·8%) with kidney failure, and 7141 (76·2%) of those with heart failure had hypertension.
sections.conclusion: One-quarter of participants had untreated or inadequately treated hypertension, reflecting the high global burden and low rates of awareness. Opportunistic May Measurement Month screening provides a low-cost, scalable route to increase awareness and detection of raised blood pressure.

items.title: Single-sequence, structure-free allosteric residue prediction with protein language models.
items.abstract: Large language models trained on protein sequences learn general coevolutionary relationships at scale, which contain useful structural and functional information. We show that attention maps, matrices of learned pairwise relationships between residues, include information about allostery. This enables prediction of allosteric relationships with no task-specific training, requiring a single input sequence and specified active-site residues, without structural information. Attention maps outperform established structure-based and sequence coevolution-based models across a benchmark of 109 allosteric proteins. In the beta-2 adrenergic receptor, a G-protein coupled receptor, attention maps correlate more strongly with experimental alanine-scanning measurements of allosteric effects on signaling than these comparators. Language model attention also guides efficient, low-throughput experimental discovery of putative allosteric residues in the protease DPP4 and residues coupled to the known allosteric pathway in ACE2. These results enable and demonstrate allosteric relationship prediction in a zero-shot, single-sequence, structure-free manner. We provide this method in the AlloGator web interface.

items.title: Microtubule Detyrosination Contributes to Altered Nuclear Mechanotransduction and Signaling in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction and is accompanied by extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, including increased desmin, tubulin, and detyrosinated tubulin levels, which we previously showed contribute to impaired relaxation. Because microtubules connect to the nucleus via the Linker of Nucleoskeleton and Cytoskeleton complex, we investigated whether cytoskeletal remodeling alters nuclear morphology, mechanics, and hypertrophy-associated signaling. Using electron microscopy and immunofluorescence in cardiac septal tissue from patients with obstructive HCM and nonfailing donors, and immunofluorescence and live-cell imaging in septal tissue from wild-type and homozygous HCM-associated Mybpc3 c.2373InsG mice, we found that nuclei were enlarged and highly invaginated, with restricted nuclear deformation during contraction, indicating altered mechanotransduction.
