In patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass, cardiovesicles capture rapid, dynamic transcriptional changes that parallel cardiomyocyte (not fibroblast, endothelial, and myeloid) responses to ischemic stress. Functional genomics implicates cardiovesicle transcripts in cardiomyocyte cell-specific cardiovascular disease liability in large human populations. Cardiovesicles may capture dynamic cardiomyocyte states in humans that reflect genetic disease liability, supporting an EV-based approach to non-invasive liquid biopsy of the myocardium.

items.title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis.
items.abstract: Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

items.title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations.
items.abstract: Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with "memory of chirality".

items.title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex.
items.abstract: Poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1-3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

items.title: Fate patterns self-organize through the coupling of structures across cell and supracellular levels of organization.
items.abstract: How patterns of cell state emerge across a tissue field is a fundamental question brought into renewed focus by spatial omics tools that map molecular states onto tissue organization. Here, we investigate how a field of limb progenitor mesenchyme transforms into distinct, adjacent cartilage and soft tissue compartments. We find that mesenchymal tissue fields self-organize their own differentiation through co-constitutive relationships between cell and supracellular structures, which produce cell-extracellular matrix (ECM) or cell-cell-based supracellular cues that canalize cartilage or soft tissue cell fate change, respectively. At the tissue level, bifurcation in intrinsically generated supracellular structures guides the specification of tissue compartment size. We find that Wnt secreted from neighboring epithelial tissue influences mesenchymal cell fate and patterning by functioning as a modulator of cell-supracellular structural coupling. Taken together, our results provide insight into how mesenchymal self-organization interfaces with epithelial signaling to robustly enable a tissue compartmentalization process that initiates the skeleton.

items.title: Autoantibody origins in lupus and upon recurrence post CAR-T therapy.
items.abstract: Anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T therapy induces profound remissions in lupus by depleting B cells, challenging the view that disease is sustained by long-lived plasma cells. Using molecular antibody tagging in mouse models of monogenic childhood-onset lupus, we show that autoantibody-producing plasma cells are short-lived and require continuous replenishment from T-bet-dependent precursors derived from long-lived B cell cohorts. The spleen is a major plasma cell reservoir, with perivascular enrichment observed in patients with lupus. Both anti-CD19 and anti-B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) CAR-T therapies eliminate anti-DNA antibodies. Recurrent autoantibodies after anti-CD19 CAR-T therapy derive exclusively from newly generated B cells, whereas those following anti-BCMA CAR-T therapy also arise from treatment-resistant clones. Thus, ongoing B cell-to-plasma cell differentiation, rather than plasma cell longevity, can sustain pathogenic antibody responses in lupus and provides a mechanistic framework for optimizing CAR-T therapies.

items.title: Neural correlates of facial recognition in a social wasp.
items.abstract: In humans and other primates, faces are special visual objects that are encoded by circuits selective to faces. If specialized circuits are the most efficient way to encode and discriminate among similar-looking objects of high relevance, then we expect that analogous circuits should evolve in other taxa with specialized visual individual recognition abilities. Thus, we surveyed the neural responses to visual objects across the brain of a wasp that has independently evolved specialized facial recognition, Polistes fuscatus. We found a localized population of neurons analogous to face cells, which we term "wasp cells," that selectively fire to front-facing wasp images. Some of these wasp cells encode information about facial patterns, which possibly underlie the unique visual recognition abilities of these wasps. These findings demonstrate high-level feature-selective tuning in an invertebrate and suggest that specialized circuits are an adaptive feature for nervous systems requiring complex visual recognition.

items.title: Right Ventricular Reverse Remodeling Without Pulmonary Vascular Unloading During Sotatercept Therapy: An Invasive Pressure-Volume Loop Study.

sections.objective: Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading.
sections.methods: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure-volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography).
sections.results: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34-67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0-65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0-42.0] mm Hg; P<0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P<0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183-242] to 160 [IQR, 129-204] mL; P<0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6-56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2-44.4] g; P<0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P=0.002). Ventricular-arterial coupling (end-systolic/arterial elastance) improved although load-independent contractility decreased alongside the decrease in effective arterial elastance. By contrast, nonresponders demonstrated a clinical-hemodynamic disconnect. Despite persistently elevated RV afterload and unchanged end-systolic/arterial elastance, a significant reduction in RV mass (56.1 [IQR, 45.9-81.0] to 46.4 [IQR, 35.9-59.4] g; P=0.003) was observed, accompanied by a significant decrease in B-type natriuretic peptide levels, whereas 6-minute walk distance did not change significantly (+15 m [95% CI, -12 to 42]; P=0.23); the difference in 6-minute walk distance change between groups did not reach significance (P=0.10). Reduction in RV mass and chamber size was observed in the absence of pulmonary vascular unloading among hemodynamic nonresponders to sotatercept in 2 independent cohorts.
sections.conclusion: In primary and validation cohorts, structural RV reverse remodeling after sotatercept initiation occurred independent of pulmonary vascular unloading. This pattern is not fully explained by pulmonary vascular unloading and raises the possibility of an effect of sotatercept on the myocardium itself. Improvement in exercise capacity was observed within the hemodynamic responder group only.

items.title: NR6A1 Drives Cardiac Remodeling by Transcriptionally Activating the Mineralocorticoid Receptor.

sections.objective: Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR/NR3C2) signaling is a central driver of pathologic cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF). The transcriptional regulation of NR3C2 and the amplification of RAAS-driven cardiac remodeling remain poorly understood.
sections.methods: Transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing data, along with HF samples from humans and mice, were used for gene expression analysis. Cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 transgenic (Nr6a1-cTG) and knockout (Nr6a1-cKO) mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction to evaluate cardiac remodeling and dysfunction. Adeno-associated virus 9-shNr3c2 was used to test whether Nr3c2 contributes to remodeling driven by Nr6a1 overexpression. Primary mouse cardiomyocytes were used for in vitro analysis. RNA sequencing, Western blot, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and luciferase assays were performed for the mechanism analysis.
sections.results: NR6A1 (nuclear receptor subfamily 6, group A, member 1) expression was increased in the heart tissue from human and mouse failing hearts. Activation of NR6A1 contributed to the hypertrophic growth of cardiomyocytes in vitro. In mice, a cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 transgene aggravated left ventricular dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis after transverse aortic constriction, whereas a cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 knockout protected the heart from failure and remodeling. Transcriptome analysis of NR6A1 downstream transcriptional targets revealed that Nr3c2 is a prominent RAAS-related downstream target in both hearts and cardiomyocytes. The transcription cofactor NR6A1 directly bound the Nr3c2 promoter, increased promoter activity, and enhanced Nr3c2 transcription in cardiomyocytes. Nr3c2 silencing attenuated NR6A1-associated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and reduced cardiac dysfunction and hypertrophy in Nr6a1-cTG mice after transverse aortic constriction. Analysis of the upstream regulation of NR6A1 in HF stress revealed that HF-related angiotensin II/AT1R signaling promoted NR6A1 expression and its downstream transcriptional and functional events in a STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1)-dependent manner.
sections.conclusion: RAAS (angiotensin II) increases the orphan receptor NR6A1, which transcriptionally activates MR/NR3C2 signaling and aggravates RAAS-associated pathologic remodeling under HF stress. This regulatory network represents an undefined feed-forward amplification mechanism linking angiotensin II signaling to MR/NR3C2 activation and may be a therapeutic target for HF with persistent MR activation.

items.title: Ambient AI documentation for structured EMR import in ophthalmology: consultation time, physician gaze behaviour and comparative accuracy.

sections.objective: EMR documentation contributes to physician workload and reduced patient-physician interaction, with ophthalmology particularly affected by specialist data requirements. This study compared ambient AI-assisted documentation for structured EMR import with conventional entry in standardised ophthalmic consultations.
sections.results: AI-assisted documentation reduced total consultation time by 2.4 min (95% CI 1.3-3.5; -32%) for the consultant and 3.0 min (95% CI 1.5-4.5; -37%) for the resident (both p = 0.002). Documentation and review time decreased by 2.3 min (95% CI 1.2-3.4; -85%) and 3.1 min (95% CI 1.6-4.5; -86%), and off-patient gaze time by 3.5 min (95% CI 2.0-4.9; -83%) and 4.1 min (95% CI 2.0-6.1; -86%), for consultant and resident, respectively (all p = 0.002). Computer-related gaze shifts decreased by 72% for both clinicians (p = 0.002). Accuracy was highest for Claude Sonnet 4.6 (98.4 ± 2.9%), followed by ChatGPT 5.3 (97.0 ± 5.1%) and Heidi 2.0.1 (88.6 ± 9.9%).
sections.conclusion: Ambient AI-assisted documentation substantially reduced consultation time, documentation burden and physician gaze metrics in ophthalmology. A two-step LLM workflow with dedicated transcription achieved the highest accuracy for structured EMR import. As only one consultant and one resident were assessed, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.
sections.other: Ten standardised ophthalmic scenarios were performed under classic and AI-assisted conditions by a consultant and a resident. ChatGPT 5.3 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 used TurboScribe transcription followed by structured LLM output; Heidi 2.0.1 used an integrated audio pipeline. All targeted structured import into an ophthalmic EMR (Heyex; Heidelberg Engineering, Heidelberg, Germany, identical to mediSIGHT; Medisoft, Leeds, UK).

items.title: Inflammatory lesions in punctate inner choroidopathy and posterior globe curvature: a widefield OCT analysis.

sections.objective: To investigate how inflammatory lesion distribution in punctate inner choroidopathy (PIC) relates to posterior globe morphology using widefield optical coherence tomography (OCT).
sections.methods: In this cross-sectional study, 62 eyes (47 with PIC and 15 fellow non-PIC eyes) from 32 patients underwent widefield swept-source OCT. Structural features, including axial length (AL), Gaussian curvature, and curvature gradient metrics, were compared between PIC and non-PIC eyes using mixed-effects models. Lesion distances to the point of maximum curvature (MC) were compared with randomly generated control points using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Lesion distribution across curvature and gradient quartiles was assessed with Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests.
sections.results: Eyes with PIC showed longer AL (29 ± 3 mm vs. 27 ± 3 mm, p = 0.001) and a higher prevalence of posterior staphyloma (62% vs. 27%, p = 0.03) than fellow non-PIC eyes. Curvature and gradient metrics did not differ significantly between groups. Across the cohort, longer AL was associated with greater curvature variability (p = 0.015) and total mean curvature gradient (p < 0.001). PIC lesions were located closer to points of maximum curvature than randomly distributed control points (p = 0.02) and were preferentially concentrated in regions of intermediate curvature and low curvature gradient (p < 0.001).
sections.conclusion: PIC preferentially occurs in highly myopic eyes with posterior staphyloma. Although global curvature metrics were primarily related to axial elongation rather than PIC status, inflammatory lesions showed a non-random spatial distribution, clustering near-but not directly over-the steepest posterior curvatures. These findings identify a reproducible association between lesion topography and posterior globe morphology and provide a framework for future longitudinal studies investigating biomechanical and vascular influences on lesion localisation.

items.title: Systematic Review of Patient Priorities and Shared Decision Making in Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease Treatment Decisions.

sections.objective: The aim of this review was to synthesise evidence on patient priorities, preferences for treatment, and shared decision making experiences in lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) treatment decisions across intermittent claudication, chronic limb threatening ischaemia, and amputation level contexts.
sections.results: Thirty-four studies were included in the systematic review, comprising qualitative, mixed methods, observational registry or cohort, and stated preference studies, and one stepped wedge cluster randomised trial. Most qualitative and cohort studies were rated moderate to high quality. Participant reporting in the 34 studies was limited: seven studies (21%) did not report sex, two (6%) recruited men only, and most mixed sex studies recruited predominantly men; and 18 (53%) did not report ethnicity and, where reported, participants were predominantly White. Across heterogeneous studies, recurring patient valued domains included pain relief, walking ability, independence, emotional wellbeing, function, quality of life, treatment burden, risk, and uncertainty. Decision making processes were shaped by preferred involvement, trust, communication, clarity of options, and continuity of care. Studies identified a mismatch between patients' preferred and experienced decisional roles, with reported involvement lower than desired. Stated preference evidence showed heterogeneity in risk tolerance and treatment trade offs. Trial evidence reported improvements in shared decision making measures and patient knowledge after structured decision support and clinician training.
sections.conclusion: Patient valued outcomes and treatment trade offs vary across lower extremity PAD contexts and individuals. Shared decision making may help incorporate these priorities into treatment decisions, supported by tailored information, continuity of care, clinician training, and decision support tools.
sections.other: Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase. This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155). Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase were searched for English language studies published from 1 January 2000 to 17 December 2025. Eligible studies included adults with symptomatic PAD, reporting experiences, information needs, priorities, or decision making related to PAD treatment. Two reviewers independently screened studies, resolving disagreements by consensus with a third reviewer. Study quality was assessed using design appropriate tools. Qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated using a structured thematic narrative approach.

items.title: Predicting Morbidity, Mortality, Revision, and Ambulation in Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputation for Peripheral Arterial Disease or Diabetes Mellitus: The Case for Regional Level Clinical Prediction Models.

sections.objective: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.
sections.methods: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.
sections.results: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.
sections.conclusion: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.

items.title: Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor for non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy without center-involving diabetic macular edema: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract: We evaluated the functional and anatomical outcomes of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy in non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy without center-involving diabetic macular edema (CI-DME), following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261319796). Four trials comprising 1228 participants were included, evaluating aflibercept, ranibizumab delivered through the Port Delivery System, and tarcocimab tedromer. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using risk ratios (RR) or mean differences (MD) for outcomes reported by at least two studies. Anti-VEGF therapy was associated with greater ≥ 2-step Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Scale (DRSS) improvement at 1 year (RR, 6.30; 95% CI, 2.80-14.16) and 2 years (RR, 3.76; 95% CI, 2.75-5.13), and lower progression to proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) with or without anterior segment neovascularization (RR, 0.11; 95% CI, 0.06-0.22 at 1 year; RR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.15-0.40 at 2 years). CI-DME development was similarly reduced (RR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.11-0.48). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) improved statistically at 1 year (MD, 0.87 letters; 95% CI, 0.30-1.43) and 2 years (MD, 0.70 letters; 95% CI, 0.02-1.38), although these differences were unlikely to be clinically meaningful. No significant difference was observed in serious ocular or non-ocular adverse events. Trial sequential analysis suggested futility for a meaningful BCVA benefit. Anti-VEGF therapy appears to improve retinopathy severity and reduce progression to PDRand CI-DME, but without a clinically meaningful visual acuity benefit. These findings warrant cautious interpretation given the heterogeneity of several pooled estimates and limited long-term randomized evidence.

items.title: High Prevalence of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Patients.

sections.objective: To evaluate the prevalence of retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) in patients with central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) and to identify factors associated with their presence.
sections.methods: Observational cross-sectional study. Two hundred forty-five patients aged 18-60 years with active CSCR and 63 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were included. RIPLs were identified using high-resolution structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) and corresponding en face OCT projections. A RIPL was defined by focal inner nuclear layer thinning with corresponding outer plexiform layer elevation and topographic perivascular correspondence on en face OCT. The presence of at least one lesion in either eye classified a participant as RIPL-positive. Demographic, systemic, clinical, and imaging characteristics were analyzed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression.
sections.results: RIPLs were identified in 85 of 245 patients with CSCR (34.7%) compared with 7 of 63 healthy controls (11.1%, P < 0.001). Bilateral RIPLs were present in 35 CSCR patients (14.3%) and 2 controls (3.2%, P = 0.028). CSCR patients with RIPLs were older, had a higher prevalence of hypertension, and had lower central retinal and subfoveal choroidal thicknesses than those without RIPLs (P < 0.05). Hypertension showed the strongest association with RIPLs presence in univariable analysis (OR 3.37, 95% CI, 1.74-6.54, P < 0.001) and remained the only independent factor in multivariable analysis (OR 2.66, 95% CI, 1.20-5.87, P = 0.016). Notably, among patients without diagnosed hypertension, RIPLs prevalence remained significantly higher than in controls (24.1% vs. 11.1%, P = 0.035).
sections.conclusion: RIPLs are highly prevalent in patients with CSCR, potentially reflecting an increased burden of cardiovascular risk factors in this cohort. This finding warrants further investigation.

items.title: Sex-Related Patterns in the Etiology and Complications of Noninfectious Uveitis: A Population-Based Cohort Study.

sections.objective: To characterize sex-related differences in the etiology, anatomic distribution, and complications of noninfectious uveitis (NIU) in a large population-based cohort.
sections.methods: Retrospective, population-based cohort study using the TriNetX federated electronic health record network. Patients with NIU diagnosed between 2010 and 2024 were identified and stratified by recorded sex. Etiologic and anatomic distributions were compared using female-to-male prevalence ratios (PRs). Seven ocular complications were compared before and after 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) on 28 covariates, with females as the reference group. Sensitivity analyses included a 91-day outcome lag, additional matching on immunomodulatory treatment, and a restricted definition of choroidal neovascular membrane.
sections.results: Of 225,607 patients, 57.9% were female (P < .001). Systemic autoimmune etiologies were more prevalent in females, including Sjögren syndrome (PR, 3.49), whereas ankylosing spondylitis (PR, 0.65) and lymphoma were more prevalent in males. Undifferentiated NIU accounted for 75.2% of NIU in males and 65.5% in females. After PSM (93,869 per cohort), male predominance was strongest for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (hazard ratio [HR], 1.90; 95% CI, 1.74-2.09; P < .001) and choroidal neovascular membrane (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.18-1.37; P < .001), and both persisted in all sensitivity analyses. Other complications had matched HRs modestly above 1 without differences in cumulative risk.
sections.conclusion: This population-level analysis confirms canonical sex-specific etiologic associations in NIU. Male sex was consistently associated with higher risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment and treated choroidal neovascular membrane. Unadjusted female-predominant complication rates may partly reflect baseline differences and healthcare utilization.

items.title: Pulmonary Function Estimation from Opportunistic Chest CT Using a Hybrid Image-plus-Quantitative-Feature Deep Learning Model.

sections.objective: Spirometry is underused and most airflow obstruction remains undiagnosed. Chest CT acquired for lung cancer screening contains anatomical and densitometric information that may proxy lung function.
sections.methods: A three-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 10,371 low-dose CT reconstructions from 5,975 National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) participants was fused with 20 lung densitometry and tracheal geometry features to predict FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. The frozen model was applied to an External Lung Cancer Screening Cohort (ELCSC, n = 268) and COPDGene (n = 10,302 scans). Ablation, two spirometric-pattern subgroups and prevalence-conditional predictive values were also evaluated. Reference spirometry was pre-bronchodilator in NLST and post-bronchodilator in COPDGene. Abnormal spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.70, FEV1 < 80% or FVC < 80% predicted) was assessed with sensitivity, specificity and AUROC, and agreement with the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC).
sections.results: The model detected abnormal spirometry with AUROC 0.898 (sensitivity 89.9%, specificity 66.1%) in the ELCSC and AUROC 0.913 (sensitivity 66.9%, specificity 96.3%) in COPDGene, with CCCs of 0.80-0.88 for FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. In held-out development data, CCCs were 0.86/0.85/0.71 (full model) versus 0.83/0.82/0.50 image-only and 0.55/0.65/0.35 feature-only. Agreement was lower, with systematic overestimation, in a COPD subgroup (FEV1/FVC < 0.70; CCC 0.62) and in a low-FVC, preserved-ratio pattern (CCC 0.70-0.78).
sections.conclusion: The model estimates spirometric parameters and detects abnormal spirometry across independent cohorts without retraining, with different sensitivity-specificity profiles at the same decision rule. It shows promise for opportunistic assessment of existing CT scans, but referral performance varies by population and prospective utility is unproven.
sections.other: Can a deep learning model combining volumetric CT with CT-derived quantitative features estimate spirometric parameters and detect abnormal spirometry in independent external cohorts without retraining?

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of the Oral Janus Kinase 1 Inhibitor Povorcitinib in Patients With Hidradenitis Suppurativa: Results of the 36-Week Open-Label Extension Period of a Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase 2 Study.

sections.objective: Treatment with povorcitinib, an oral, selective Janus kinase 1 inhibitor, improved lesions and symptoms in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) during the 16-week placebo-controlled period of a phase 2 study. Assess efficacy and safety of povorcitinib during the 36-week open-label extension (OLE).
sections.methods: All patients received once-daily povorcitinib 75 mg. Assessments included change from baseline in abscess and inflammatory nodule (AN) count, draining tunnel (dT) count, HS Clinical Response (HiSCR), International HS Severity Score System (IHS4), patient-reported outcomes, flare frequency, and safety. Efficacy outcomes (descriptive analyses) were evaluated using observed-case (all endpoints) and last-observation-carried-forward (select endpoints).
sections.results: 175 patients entered OLE. Sustained improvements through Week 52 occurred in all efficacy and patient-reported outcomes, including AN count (mean [SD], -65.7% [41.2]), dT count (-51.1% [72.4]), Skin Pain (-26.9% [84.6]), and HiSQoL (-33.5% [65.3]). HiSCR100 rates ranged from 22.2%-29.4% and IHS4-100 20.0%-29.4%. HS flares occurred in 19.7% of patients. Common adverse events were COVID-19 and acne; 4 herpes zoster (all grade ≤2) and 10 serious adverse events (none treatment-related) occurred.
sections.conclusion: Efficacy and quality-of-life outcomes were maintained through 1 year of povorcitinib 75 mg treatment, with a favorable benefit-risk balance.
sections.other: Lack of control arm.

items.title: Expression of GPX4 and redox balance are critical for intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes homeostasis.
items.abstract: Intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) provide frontline mucosal defense while functioning within a hypoxic epithelial niche characterized by sustained oxidative stress. Their distinctive mitochondrial and metabolic features may predispose them to oxidative damage; however, how IELs maintain viability under these conditions remains unclear. Here we showed that IELs engaged robust antioxidant transcriptional programs and identified glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) as a cell-intrinsic factor selectively required for IEL maintenance. Conditional deletion of Gpx4 in CD8+ T cells or TCRαβ+ T cells caused profound loss of IELs, without affecting peripheral T cell compartments. Gpx4-deficient IELs accumulated reactive oxygen species, underwent lipid peroxidation and succumbed to ferroptotic cell death, a phenotype rescued by vitamin E supplementation. Functionally, loss of Gpx4 increased susceptibility to enteric infection in mice, while reduced GPX4 expression was associated with pathology of inflammatory bowel disease in humans, establishing GPX4-dependent control of ferroptosis as a central mechanism sustaining IEL survival and intestinal barrier immunity.

items.title: Beyond Calcium: CT Phenotyping of Fibrocalcific Aortic Stenosis.
items.abstract: Aortic stenosis is characterized by progressive fibrocalcific remodeling driven by inflammation, fibrosis, and calcification. Although echocardiography and noncontrast computed tomographic calcium scoring (aortic valve calcium score) remain the clinical standards for hemodynamic and structural assessment, computed tomographic angiography, already routinely performed for transcatheter aortic valve replacement planning, provides complementary tissue-level characterization of fibrotic and calcific valve remodeling. Artificial intelligence is increasingly being applied to facilitate the quantitative assessment of fibrocalcific burden and periaortic adipose tissue inflammation. This review examines emerging applications of computed tomographic angiography for fibrocalcific tissue characterization, inflammatory phenotyping, and artificial intelligence-enabled risk assessment in aortic stenosis and discusses their potential role in complementing conventional hemodynamic assessment.

items.title: Agents targeting the hallmarks of ageing: the geroscience pipeline in 2026.
items.abstract: The hallmarks of ageing provide a conceptual framework for therapeutic development. We searched ClinicalTrials.gov for registered clinical trials that were ongoing as of Jan 1, 2026, and investigated pharmacological and biological agents targeting one or more hallmarks of ageing. Eligible trials were ongoing and involved adults (aged ≥18 years) and tested pharmacological or biological agents or products targeting one or more hallmarks of ageing. The search involved three steps with a focus on identifying trials conducted outside the context of a specific disease, to identify studies aimed at delaying biological ageing and preventing age-related functional decline; identifying trials assessing interventions targeting the most prevalent age-related diseases; and a further search using the names of the agents identified in the first two steps. We included 193 trials investigating 131 candidate treatments. Of these, 41 (21%) involved healthy individuals or individuals at risk of functional decline, and 152 (79%) targeted established age-related diseases. Most trials were early phase, comprising Phase 1 (61 [32%]) and Phase 2 (91 [47%]), and 41 (21%) were Phase 3. Altered intercellular communication was the most frequently targeted hallmark (64 [33%]), followed by deregulated nutrient sensing (48 [25%]), chronic inflammation (32 [17%]), and stem cell exhaustion (26 [13%]). Our findings show that although many ongoing trials target biological mechanisms considered hallmarks of ageing, most studies are in early phases and mainly aim to treat age-related diseases rather than to delay or prevent age-related decline.

items.title: Safety and immunogenicity of a trivalent vaccine candidate against invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease and typhoid fever in healthy adults in Europe and Africa: a phase 1/2a randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) disease and typhoid fever are major public health concerns in Africa. Although typhoid conjugate vaccines (TCVs) are available, there is no licensed vaccine against iNTS. We aimed to investigate the safety and immunogenicity of a trivalent vaccine candidate (iNTS-TCV) comprising a monovalent TCV and a bivalent vaccine candidate against Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium and Salmonella enterica serovar Enteritidis, developed with generalised modules for membrane antigens (GMMA) technology (iNTS-GMMA).
sections.methods: This phase 1/2a randomised controlled trial was done at two study sites: Belgium (stage 1) and Malawi (stage 2). Healthy adults (aged 18-50 years) with no known previous exposure to or vaccination against Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S Typhi) or iNTS, or both, who provided informed consent were randomly assigned according to a block randomisation schedule (block size of five in stage 1 and seven in stage 2) generated by an independent statistician (2:2:1 in stage 1 and 3:3:1 in stage 2) to receive separate injections in different arms on days 1, 57, and 169. In stage 1, participants received low-dose or full-dose iNTS-TCV and saline, low-dose or full-dose iNTS-GMMA + TCV, or placebo and saline; in stage 2, participants received full-dose iNTS-TCV and saline, full-dose iNTS-GMMA + TCV, or one of three control vaccines and saline at each vaccination timepoint. Participants, site staff, investigators, and the sponsor were all masked to group assignments. The primary outcome was the safety and reactogenicity of the iNTS-TCV vaccine: solicited events occurring 7 days post-vaccination, unsolicited adverse events occurring 28 days post-vaccination, serious adverse events, adverse events or serious adverse events leading to study withdrawal or study intervention discontinuation from day 1 to 197, and laboratory test results 7 days and 28 days post-vaccination. Secondary outcomes included all serious adverse events as well as adverse events and serious adverse events leading to discontinuation from the study from day 197 to 337 (end of study), and immunogenicity. Safety was assessed in all participants who received at least one study dose (exposed set); immunogenicity was assessed in all participants who received all doses as per protocol and had post-dose immunogenicity results available (per-protocol set). The completed trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05480800).
sections.results: Between Sept 13, 2022, and Feb 2, 2024, 50 participants were randomly assigned in stage 1 (four in the low-dose iNTS-TCV group, four in the low-dose iNTS-GMMA + TCV group, 16 in the full-dose iNTS-TCV group, 16 in the full-dose iNTS-GMMA + TCV group, and ten in the placebo group) and 105 were randomly assigned in stage 2 (45 in the full-dose iNTS-TCV group, 45 in the full-dose iNTS-GMMA + TCV group, and 15 in the control group). In stage 1, solicited events occurred in all participants in investigational groups versus nine of ten (90·0%; 95% CI 55·5-99·7) in the placebo group; in stage 2, solicited events occurred in 41 of 45 (91·1%; 78·8-97·5) participants in the iNTS-TCV full-dose group and 45 of 45 (100·0%; 92·1-100·0) participants in the iNTS-GMMA + TCV full-dose group versus 13 of 15 (86·7%; 59·5-98·3) in the control group. In stage 1, unsolicited adverse events occurred in 15 of 16 (93·8%; 95% CI 69·8-99·8) participants in each full-dose group, versus eight of ten (80·0%; 44·4-97·5) in the placebo group; in stage 2, unsolicited adverse events occurred in 29 of 45 (64·4%; 48·8-78·1) participants in the iNTS-TCV full-dose group and 33 of 45 (73·3%; 58·1-85·4) in the iNTS-GMMA + TCV full-dose group versus nine of 15 (60·0%; 32·3-83·7) in the control group. In stage 1, two adverse events leading to vaccine discontinuation occurred. No serious adverse events related to study vaccinations occurred. After each dose, most participants had laboratory test values within reference ranges. After dose 1, iNTS-TCV and iNTS-GMMA + TCV full doses induced robust IgG responses against all vaccine antigens.
sections.conclusion: iNTS-TCV did not raise any safety concerns and showed immunogenicity, supporting further clinical assessment in target age groups.

items.title: Real-World 30-day Outcomes Following Commercial Adoption of the GORE EXCLUDER Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis: A National Medicare Analysis.

sections.objective: The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.
sections.methods: Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries undergoing TAMBE between October 2024 and December 2025 were identified using the TAMBE-specific ICD-10-PCS code (X2VE3SA). Outcomes were compared to a contemporaneous cohort undergoing ≥4-vessel F/BEVAR in 2023, the year preceding TAMBE approval. Primary outcomes included 30-day mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), acute kidney injury (AKI), spinal cord ischemia (SCI), bowel ischemia, and reintervention, and were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regressions with adjustment for demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics. Pre-specified sub-analyses examined outcomes by aortic indication, hospital procedure volume, and adoption period. Consistent with CMS small-cell suppression policy, any outcome frequencies <11 events were masked and not reported.
sections.results: The primary cohort consisted of 869 patients treated at 351 hospitals, compared with 678 patients undergoing 4-vessel F/BEVAR. TAMBE was associated with significantly higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (6.7% vs. 4.0%; P=.02), though this difference did not persist after adjustment (adjusted HR 1.37 [0.85-2.21]). No differences were observed in stroke ( .05). The majority of implanting hospitals (N=195; 56%) performed a single TAMBE during the study period, and 30-day outcomes did not differ significantly by hospital volume after adjustment. A sensitivity analysis restricted to unambiguously coded, elective TAMBE cases compared with elective F/BEVAR showed similarly elevated 30-day mortality (6.8% vs. 4.0%), albeit not statistically different following adjustment (aHR 1.46 [0.75-2.84]).
sections.conclusion: In this national analysis of Medicare FFS beneficiaries, real-world 30-day outcomes following TAMBE in the first year-plus of commercial availability were notably worse than those reported in the pivotal trial and early single-institution post-market series, with a nearly 7% 30-day mortality rate that persisted across indications, hospital volumes, and time periods. The rapid dissemination of TAMBE to over 351 hospitals, most performing only a single procedure, highlights a fundamental tension between the device's off-the-shelf accessibility and the institutional readiness required for safe deployment, underscoring the need for ongoing post-market surveillance, structured proctorship programs, and a more deliberate approach to patient and operator selection as TAMBE adoption continues.

items.title: Retinal deposits: A narrative review of genetic causes and their phenocopies.
items.abstract: Retinal deposits represent a structurally convergent but biologically heterogeneous manifestation of numerous inherited retinal diseases and frequently pose a diagnostic challenge because similar funduscopic phenotypes may arise from distinct genetic and molecular mechanisms. We performed a structured narrative review of the literature to synthesize the genetic causes of sub-retinal, sub-retinal pigment epithelium, and intraretinal deposit phenotypes, with emphasis on molecular pathophysiology, anatomical localization on optical coherence tomography, characteristic imaging features, and natural history. Across disease groups, deposits were found to result from diverse mechanisms, including visual cycle dysfunction, impaired photoreceptor outer segment processing, extracellular matrix and Bruch membrane abnormalities, lipid metabolic defects, and crystalline metabolite accumulation. Despite overlapping clinical appearances such as vitelliform material, flecks, drusen-like lesions, or crystalline deposits, optical coherence tomography allows consistent compartmental classification relative to the retinal pigment epithelium, which in turn correlates with underlying biology and genotype. Visual cycle-related flecked retina disorders demonstrate progressive rod dysfunction distinct from stationary phenotypes, while sub-retinal pigment epithelium deposits in monogenic macular dystrophies may mimic age-related macular degeneration, but differ in age of onset, inheritance pattern, and complication risk. Recognition of these genotype-deposit correlations and application of a compartment-based classification may improve differential diagnosis; guide targeted genetic testing and support the development of imaging biomarkers relevant to emerging gene-directed therapies.

items.title: Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut-brain interaction.
items.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.

items.title: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.

sections.objective: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).
sections.methods: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116.
sections.results: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group.
sections.conclusion: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

items.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
sections.methods: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. The data cutoff date was March 23, 2026. Progression-free survival and overall survival were evaluated as dual primary endpoints using a graphical multiple-testing approach with prespecified alpha allocation. Progression-free survival was assessed every 8 weeks through to week 56, then every 12 weeks thereafter; overall survival was assessed continuously. The safety analysis included all randomly assigned patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. For progression-free survival, missing radiographic assessments were handled using prespecified censoring rules; no imputation was performed for missing overall survival or safety data. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06132958) and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Jan 5, 2024, and Sept 17, 2025, 776 patients were randomly assigned to sac-TMT (n=386) or TPC (n=390). 384 (99%) of 386 patients in the sac-TMT group and 367 (94%) of 390 in the TPC group received at least one dose of study treatment. At data cutoff, median follow-up was 14·0 months (IQR 11·0-16·9). Median progression-free survival was 7·2 months (95% CI 5·6-7·6) in the sac-TMT group and 3·9 months (3·7-5·3) in the TPC group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·50-0·70]; p<0·0001) and median overall survival was 19·0 months (16·1-not reached) in the sac-TMT group and 12·1 months (11·0-15·2) in the TPC group (0·68 [0·55-0·84]; p=0·0001). 265 (69%) of 384 patients in the sac-TMT group and 210 (57%) of 367 in the TPC group had a grade 3 or higher adverse event. Serious adverse events were reported in 133 (35%) patients in the sac-TMT group and 117 (32%) patients in the TPC group. Treatment-related adverse events led to death in three (<1%) patients in the sac-TMT group and three (<1%) in the TPC group.
sections.conclusion: Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

items.title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.

sections.objective: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.
sections.methods: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.
sections.results: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns.
sections.conclusion: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

items.title: Migraine.
items.abstract: Migraine is a chronic neurovascular disorder characterised by recurrent attacks of moderate-to-severe head pain, accompanied by transient but disabling symptoms such as aura, nausea, vomiting, phonophobia, and photophobia, reflecting the involvement of multiple systems. Migraine affects and disables a large proportion of the global population. The pathogenesis of migraine involves the interplay of genetic and epigenetic factors across complex neurosensory and neurovascular networks. Decades of research have elucidated key components of these pathways, driving the development of mechanism-based therapies that are now transforming clinical practice and substantially improving patients' lives.

items.title: Safety and clinical outcomes of cataract surgery follow-up at urban hospitals versus rural vision centres.

sections.objective: Distance to healthcare facilities is a barrier to follow-up adherence after cataract surgery in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated the effectiveness of decentralised postoperative care at rural vision centres compared to urban hospital-based follow-up after cataract surgery.
sections.methods: Eyes that underwent cataract surgery at Aravind Eye Hospital Pondicherry, India (urban hospital) from July 1st, 2022 to June 30th, 2023 were reviewed. Patients received postoperative month one (POM1) follow-up at either the urban hospital or one of 12 rural vision centres. Variables collected included demographics, payment type, surgical details, complications, preoperative UCVA, postoperative day one (POD1) and postoperative month one (POM1) best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and IOP. Predictors of good visual outcome (BCVA ≥ 6/12) were assessed.
sections.results: Of 46,624 eyes, 87.1% (N = 40,619) received POM1 postoperative follow-up at the urban hospital and 12.9% (N = 6,005) at a vision centre. Vision centre patients were more often female, received subsidised care, and had better preoperative VA (p < 0.001). At POM1, BCVA was 6/6-6/18 in 94.9% of urban hospital eyes and 94.2% of vision centre eyes. Eyes receiving vision centre follow-up had fewer cases of BCVA < 6/60 (0.3% vs. 1.2%, p < 0.001). Postoperative infection rates were low across groups (0.02%). Adjusted analyses showed vision centre follow-up was associated with higher odds of good visual outcome ( ≥ 6/12) (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.37-1.63, p < 0.001).
sections.conclusion: Decentralised follow-up at vision centres was non-inferior to urban hospitals in POM1 VA and infection rates. Vision centres offer a scalable solution to improve access to cataract care without compromising safety.

items.title: Retinal Structure Reflects Cumulative Blast Exposure and Blast-Related Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.

sections.objective: U.S. military service members experienced a high rate of blast exposures during post-9/11 military conflicts. Though a growing body of literature suggests that these exposures have long term consequences for health, objective biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma remain limited. We used optical coherence tomography (OCT) to determine whether blast-related mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) and cumulative blast exposure burden were associated with retinal microstructural changes.
sections.methods: A retrospective, cross-sectional cohort study at VA Boston Healthcare System. Seventy-three United States post 9/11 veterans enrolled in the Translational Research Center for TBI & Stress Disorders (TRACTS) longitudinal cohort study who underwent OCT imaging based on assessment availability. Principal observations were blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and cumulative lifetime blast exposure burden.
sections.results: Among 73 participants (mean [SD] age, 40.8 [9.4] years; 63 [86%] male), 25 had a history of blast mTBI (blast mTBI+) and 48 did not (blast mTBI-). Participants with blast mTBI+ had significantly thicker retinal layers in the macula, specifically in the 3mm quadrants around the fovea. The peripapillary RNFL (pRNFL) was significantly thinner in the blast mTBI+ group (p = .009), with the most significant thinning occurring nasally, most notably superior/nasal (p < .001). Greater cumulative blast exposure burden was associated with lower pRNFL thickness (ρ = -.288, p = .013) and greater macular outer retinal layer thickness (ρ = .319, p = .007). In cross-validated predictive analyses, pRNFL, outer plexiform layer, and outer retinal layer thickness significantly predicted cumulative blast exposure burden (leave-one-subject-out correlation, r = .335; conditional Monte Carlo permutation p = .005, full discovery Monte Carlo permutation p = .021).
sections.conclusion: Retinal structural measures distinguished veterans with blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and predicted cumulative blast exposure burden. These findings support OCT as an accessible approach for identifying retinal biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma and cumulative blast exposure.
sections.other: Retinal thickness as measured by high-resolution Spectralis OCT imaging, including 7 individual macular layers, combined macular layers (inner retina, outer retina, and total retina), and the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer, using automated segmentation software.

items.title: Association Between Adjunctive Single-Ingredient Diosmin Prescribing and Short-Term Clinical Outcomes in Acute Lower-Extremity Superficial Vein Thrombosis.

sections.objective: To estimate the association between documented adjunctive single-ingredient diosmin prescribing and short-term clinical outcomes in adults with acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis.
sections.methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective 48-hour landmark cohort study of 1,820 consecutive adults with duplex-confirmed acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis treated from January 1, 2021, through December 31, 2025. Exposure was a diosmin prescription issued within 48 hours and intended for at least 7 days. The primary outcome was complete resolution or marked clinical improvement at the in-person assessment closest to day 14 within days 10 to 18. Missing baseline covariates were multiply imputed, and propensity scores were estimated within 20 imputed data sets. Stabilized inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting targeted the average treatment effect under measured-confounding assumptions. Secondary outcomes, including day-7 pain, were exploratory.
sections.results: Diosmin was prescribed to 910 patients and not prescribed to 910. Primary improvement occurred in 728/910 (80.0%) and 669/910 (73.5%), respectively. Weighted standardized probabilities were 79.5% (95% confidence interval, 76.8%-82.2%) and 74.7% (71.8%-77.6%), yielding a risk difference of 4.8 percentage points (1.2-8.4) and a risk ratio of 1.06 (1.01-1.12). The E-value was 1.31 for the point estimate and 1.11 for the confidence limit. Excluding 142 patients with concomitant distal deep vein thrombosis gave a similar estimate (risk difference, 4.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 1.3-8.5). Exploratory day-7 pain-response probabilities were 75.0% and 61.5% after imputation, weighting, and marginal standardization. Thrombotic and bleeding estimates were imprecise.
sections.conclusion: Documented adjunctive diosmin prescribing was associated with a small increase in short-term clinical improvement. Clinical importance is uncertain, and relatively weak unmeasured confounding could explain the primary association. The exploratory pain finding is hypothesis-generating. These data are insufficient to support routine diosmin use or substitution for guideline-directed anticoagulation; adequately powered randomized trials are needed.

items.title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis Demonstrates Excellent Outcomes: A Decade Review of Three Stroke Centers.

sections.objective: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers.
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study. We analyzed CEA and TCAR procedures for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis from January 2017 through February 2026 across three institutions. One-to-one nearest-neighbor propensity score matching was performed without replacement. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Cox regression with robust variance estimates. Fine-Gray regression was used to treat death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes.
sections.results: The final cohort included 889 procedures, 750 CEAs and 139 TCARs. Matching yielded 136 balanced pairs. No ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), myocardial infarction (MI), or death occurred within 30 days after TCAR, and no 30-day outcome differed significantly between matched groups. In adjusted analyses of the full cohort, TCAR was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.31), stroke or death (aHR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.13-2.36), and the composite of TIA, stroke, MI, or death (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.11-2.24). After matching, these associations did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 4.0 years. Long-term neurologic outcomes also did not differ significantly. Restenosis did not differ significantly (subdistribution HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.62-3.30; P = 0.399), and one reintervention occurred in each matched group.
sections.conclusion: Among selected asymptomatic patients, TCAR had low perioperative event rates. After matching, no significant differences from CEA were detected in long-term neurologic outcomes, mortality, composite outcomes, restenosis, or reintervention, while late MI remained higher after TCAR. These findings support TCAR as an attractive revascularization option when CEA is less suitable.

items.title: When Hip Pain Is Vascular: Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysmal Lesion in Behçet's Disease Treated with a Covered Stent.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease is a chronic relapsing systemic vasculitis in which arterial involvement is less common than venous disease but carries substantial rupture risk. Internal iliac artery involvement is rare and may be overlooked because symptoms are often nonspecific. We report a 34-year-old man with established Behçet's disease referred from orthopaedic surgery after 2 to 3 months of right hip and deep gluteal pain initially considered musculoskeletal. Plain hip x-ray was unremarkable. Pelvic imaging demonstrated a right pelvic arterial lesion, and computed tomography angiography (CTA) confirmed a 57 mm saccular aneurysmal lesion arising from the right internal iliac artery. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and perioperative immunosuppression was optimized with rheumatology input. Endovascular repair was performed via contralateral left common femoral access using a 6 × 60 mm self-expanding covered stent graft across the diseased internal iliac segment, without adjunctive coil embolization. Completion angiography showed complete sac exclusion with preserved distal internal iliac flow. Recovery was uneventful. One-month CTA confirmed persistent exclusion and stent-graft patency, and the patient remained clinically asymptomatic at 12 months. This case highlights an orthopaedic mimic and supports carefully selected flow-preserving endovascular repair under immunosuppressive cover, with lifelong imaging surveillance to detect late complications in this inflammatory disease setting.Clinical ImpactInternal iliac artery aneurysmal lesions are rare manifestations of vascular Behçet's disease and may present with hip, buttock or groin pain due to deep pelvic mass effect, leading to initial orthopaedic referral and potential diagnostic delay. This case emphasizes the need to consider a vascular cause in Behçet's disease patients with unexplained persistent pelvic or hip pain, especially when plain radiographs are normal. It also illustrates a flow-preserving endovascular strategy using a covered stent graft to exclude the lesion while maintaining internal iliac artery patency. Because Behçet's disease is an inflammatory vasculitis, technical success alone is insufficient; perioperative immunosuppression and lifelong clinical and imaging surveillance remain central to management.

items.title: One-Year Results From the EMBRACE Registry Evaluating the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis during BEVAR for Complex Abdominal and Thoracoabdominal Aneurysms.

sections.objective: The stability of bridging stents is critical to ensure the effectiveness and safety of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA). The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR.
sections.methods: The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up. Patients were divided into BEVAR and fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) arms. This analysis reports the BEVAR cohort, which included patients receiving the VBX Stent Graft as a bridging stent for at least 1 visceral vessel. The primary endpoint was patient-level primary patency at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included technical success, reintervention, and target vessel patency assessed annually for up to 5 years. Secondary safety outcomes included major adverse events and aneurysm-related mortality.
sections.results: A total of 165 patients (69.1% male, mean age 72.5 ± 9 years) were enrolled, receiving 454 VBX Stent Grafts (26.0% celiac trunk, 28.9% superior mesenteric artery (SMA), 21.8% left renal, and 23.3% right renal artery). VBX Stent Graft technical success was 99.6%. Thirty-day mortality was 7.9%, with major adverse events in 15.2% (1.8% respiratory failure, 7.3% renal function deterioration, 0.6% bowel ischemia, 4.2% paraplegia, and 1.8% major stroke). Freedom from aneurysm-related mortality was 92.1% at 30 days and 90.2% at 1 year. Freedom from patient-level VBX-related reintervention was 91.7%. Patient-level primary patency and secondary patency were 97.7% and 98.5%, respectively. Freedom from target vessel instability at the patient level was 90.4%.
sections.conclusion: Short-term findings from this multicenter registry confirm that the VBX Stent Graft is a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR, demonstrating high technical success, excellent 1-year patency, and low rates of target vessel instability. Ongoing follow-up will evaluate mid-term durability.Clinical ImpactBridging stent performance is fundamental to the success of branched endovascular repair, yet multicenter, real-world data remain limited. This analysis from the EMBRACE registry demonstrates high technical reliability, excellent 1-year target vessel patency, and low rates of VBX Stent Graft-related reintervention. Technical failures were uncommon and were primarily associated with inadequate distal landing zones, highlighting the importance of procedural planning. These findings provide clinicians with contemporary evidence supporting the VBX Stent Graft as a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR and may inform procedural decision-making to optimize target vessel durability.

items.title: The effects of size and sex mismatch on kidney functional adaption following living donor kidney transplantation.

sections.objective: The remarkable functional adaption of transplanted kidneys is poorly understood. Conflicting results for donor-recipient body size and sex mismatches, and concerns for hyperfiltration injury are unresolved.
sections.methods: This single center, longitudinal cohort study of 194 living kidney transplantations evaluated changes in isotopic 9 9mTc-DTPA measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR) from side-specific donor function at implantation through 12-months after transplantation against multiple anthropometric parameters, sex mismatch, and pathological hyperfiltration.
sections.results: Donor kidney mGFR was predicted by younger age, male sex, and heavier body weight using multivariable analysis; and strongly influenced 12-month mGFR. Post-transplant relative and absolute mGFR changes were determined by donor and recipient body sizes (weight, body surface area, and body mass index were statistically interchangeable) and donor and recipient sex using multivariable analysis. mGFR adaption was greatest in smaller female donor kidneys transplanted into large male recipients, but negligible or negative for male kidneys into female recipients. The mGFR ratio significantly correlated with mismatch in donor-recipient body surface area (r=0.285) and body mass index (r=0.248). Absolute mGFR significantly increased with recipient lean body mass (r=0.425) but not total fat content using body composition analysis. Diabetes, fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin A1c, androgenic hormones, and hypertension were unrelated. Evidence of significant maladaptive glomerular hyperfiltration assessed by albuminuria, glomerular pathology, percentage glomerulosclerosis, glomerulomegaly, transcription factor WT1 podocyte immunostaining, chronic interstitial fibrosis, and ultrastructural podocyte effacement at 12-months was absent. Death-censored graft survivals for five-, 10-, and 20-years after transplantation were excellent at 96.9%, 94.3%, and 80.8%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: mGFR following transplantation depends on input donor quality with adaption driven primarily by larger recipient body size mismatch and male sex. Functional adaption appears as a benign physiological response appropriately calibrated to individual recipient metabolic need without evidence of pathological hyperfiltration injury.

items.title: Complex Endovascular Repair for Genetically-Triggered Aortic Disease in Italy (CENTRAL Multicentric Registry).

sections.objective: The role of fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) in patients with genetically triggered aortic disease and connective tissue disorders (CTDs) remains controversial due to concerns regarding long-term durability and disease progression. This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).
